sctrls.name: AfterImage
sctrls.description: Enables player afterimage effects. The character's frames are stored in a history buffer, and are displayed after a delay as afterimages.

params.name: time
params.description: Specifies the number of ticks that the afterimages should be displayed for. Set to -1 to display indefinitely. Defaults to 1.

params.name: length
params.description: Sets the capacity of the frame history buffer. The history will hold up to *no_of_frames* of the character's most recently saved frames. Assuming constant values for timegap and framegap, increasing the length can increase the number and `age` (for lack of a better term) of afterimages displayed at one time. The maximum length is 60, and the default is 20.

params.name: palpostbright
params.description: These parameters determine palette effects to be applied to all afterimages. First the color level is adjusted according to the palcolor value, then if invertall is non-zero the colors are inverted. Afterwards, the palbright components are added to the corresponding component of the player's palette, then each component is multiplied by the corresponding palcontrast component divided by 256, then the palpostbright components are added to the result. The value of palcolor ranges from 0 (greyscale) to 256 (normal color). For instance, if the red component of the character's palette is denoted *pal_r*, then the red component of the afterimage palette is given by (*pal_r* + *add_r*) \* *mul_r*…

params.name: palmul
params.description: These parameters specify palette effects that are applied repeatedly to successive frames in the afterimage. In one application of these palette effects, first the paladd components are added to the afterimage palette, then the components are multiplied by the palmul multipliers. These effects are applied zero times to the most recent afterimage frame, once to the second-newest afterimage frame, twice in succession to the third-newest afterimage frame, etc. Valid values are 0-255 for the paladd components, and any non-negative float value for the palmul multipliers. The defaults are:

params.name: timegap
params.description: This parameter controls how many frames to skip between saving player frames to the history buffer for afterimage display. The default is 1 (skip no frames). To save every third frame (for example), you would use timegap = 3.

params.changeNote:
Not a direct parameter adjustment, but if the character has `ikemenVersion` it receives some bug fixes that make afterimages work as expected.

For instance, for parameter values of `framegap = 5` and `length = 20`:
- A Mugen character will show afterimages for the 0th, 4th, 9th and 14th recorded frames.
- An Ikemen character will show afterimages for the 5th, 10th, 15th and 20th recorded frames.
params.name: framegap
params.description: Every *value*'th frame in the history buffer will be displayed as an afterimage. For instance, if framegap = 4 (the default), then the first, fifth, ninth, ... frames of the history buffer will be displayed as afterimages.

params.name: trans
params.description: Specifies the transparency type for the afterimages. Valid values for *type* are `none` for an opaque afterimage, `add`, `add1`, and `sub`. Defaults to `none`.

params.name: palinvertblend
params.description:
Inverts current blend mode if enabled so Sub becomes Add and Add becomes Sub.

For PalFx it accepts 4 values:
* 0 = Disabled (Mugen 1.0 blending behavior)
* 1 = Enabled (Mugen 1.0 blending behavior)
* -1 = Disabled (Mugen 1.1 blending behavior)
* 2 = Enabled (Mugen 1.1 blending behavior)

If character MugenVersion is 1.1 and invertall = 1 and if invertblend param is omitted, it inverts blend by default. For all other MugenVersion invertblend is 0 if omitted.

params.name: shader.name
params.description: Specifying the name of the currently loaded custom shader will apply that shader to the Afterimage.

params.name: shader.paramX
params.description: Specifies the value to send to the custom shader. The value specified here can be used as a variable within the custom shader. X is limited to 0 to 15, and a maximum of 16 values ​​can be sent.

params.name: shader.playerno
params.description: Specifies the player number who owns the shader to be used. Defaults to own player number.

sctrls.name: AfterImageTime
sctrls.description: Changes the duration of the player's afterimage effects, if currently enabled. If no afterimage effects are being displayed, this controller does nothing. Known bugs: If the timegap parameter in the originating AfterImage controller is not set at 1, using this AfterImageTime will cause the frame positions to be reset.

params.name: time
params.description: Sets the new number of ticks that the afterimages will be displayed before being removed.

sctrls.name: AllPalFX
sctrls.description: Same as PalFX, except that this affects the palette of the background and lifebars as well as the palette of all characters and explods (regardless of the ownpal parameter). See the PalFX section for details on the parameters to AllPalFX.

params.name: invertblend
params.description:
Inverts current blend mode if enabled so Sub becomes Add and Add becomes Sub.

For AllPalFx it accepts 2 values:
* 0 = Disabled (Mugen 1.0 blending behavior)
* 1 = Enabled (Mugen 1.1 blending behavior)

Defaults to 0 if omitted. If 1 it inverts blending on chars "layer".

sctrls.name: AngleAdd
sctrls.description: Adds to the drawing rotation angle used by AngleDraw.

params.name: value
params.description: *add_angle* should be given in degrees.

sctrls.name: AngleDraw
sctrls.description: Draws the player (for 1 frame) rotated about his axis by the angle set by the AngleSet controller. When facing right, a positive angle means a counterclockwise rotation.

params.name: value
params.description: Sets the drawing angle in degrees.

params.name: scale
params.description: Scales the player sprite.

params.name: pivot
params.description: Shifts the sprite's rotation center by the specified x and y offsets.

sctrls.name: AngleMul
sctrls.description: Multiplies the drawing rotation angle used by AngleDraw by the specified factor.

params.name: value
params.description: Multiplies the drawing angle by *angle_multiplier*.

sctrls.name: AngleSet
sctrls.description: Sets the drawing rotation angle used by AngleDraw. The angle is initialized at 0.

params.name: value
params.description: The value of *angle* is interpreted to be in degrees.

sctrls.name: AppendToClipboard
sctrls.description: This is the same as DisplayToClipboard, except that message text is added on a new line, instead of overwriting whatever text is already on the clipboard. See DisplayToClipboard for a format description.
changeNotes: Unlike Mugen, Ikemen GO can use unlimited amount of numeric arguments. Also it supports format specifiers, e.g. %0.2f (prints float value truncated to 2 digits), %v (prints the value in a default format and optimal formatting, regardless if it's int, float or string).

sctrls.name: AssertAnalogVector
sctrls.description: This controller allows (de)activating the player's analog vectors without input from a joystick. Values will be clamped to `[-1,1]` with the exception of analog triggers which are normalized to `[0,1]`.

params.name: leftx
params.description: Sets the `LeftX` analog vector. Defaults to 0.

params.name: lefty
params.description: Sets the `LeftY` analog vector. Defaults to 0.

params.name: rightx
params.description: Sets the `RightX` analog vector. Defaults to 0.

params.name: righty
params.description: Sets the `RightY` analog vector. Defaults to 0.

params.name: lefttrigger
params.description: Sets the `LeftTrigger` analog vector. Defaults to 0.

params.name: righttrigger
params.description: Sets the `RightTrigger` analog vector. Defaults to 0.

sctrls.example:
[State -1, AssertAnalogVector]
type = AssertAnalogVector
leftx = 0.125
lefty = -0.5
rightx = 0
righty = 0
lefttrigger = 0.75
righttrigger = 0

sctrls.name: AssertCommand
sctrls.description: This controller allows (de)activating the player's commands without any button presses. If the player has multiple commands with the same name, the controller will affect all of them.

params.name: name
params.description: Command to assert.

params.name: buffer.time
params.description: Number of ticks to buffer the command. Defaults to 1.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = AssertCommand
trigger1 = time = 10
name = "QCF_x"
buffer.time = 5

sctrls.name: AssertInput
sctrls.description: This controller allows you to assert up to three input flags simultaneously via single sctrl. Similarly to AssertSpecial, there is no limit how many times this controller is called. Each flag will be automatically "de-asserted" at every game tick, so you must assert a flag for each tick that you want it to be active. Ikemen interprets input flags the same was as if corresponding input keys were pressed.

params.name: flag
params.description: String specifying the flag to assert.

params.name: flag2
params.description: An optional flag to assert.

params.name: flag3
params.description: Another optional flag to assert.

params.name: flag4
params.description: Another optional flag to assert.

params.name: flag5
params.description: Another optional flag to assert.

params.name: flag6
params.description: Another optional flag to assert.

params.name: flag7
params.description: Another optional flag to assert.

params.name: flag8
params.description: Another optional flag to assert.

sctrls.name: AssertSpecial
sctrls.description: This controller allows you to assert up to three special flags simultaneously. MUGEN will automatically `deassert` each flag at every game tick, so you must assert a flag for each tick that you want it to be active.

params.changeNote: AssertSpecial now allows setting up to 8 flags at a time.
params.name: flag
params.description: *flag_name* is a string specifying the flag to assert.

params.name: flag2
params.description: An optional flag to assert.

params.name: flag3
params.description: Another optional flag to assert.

params.name: Enabled
params.description: Setting this parameter to 0 will disable the specified flags instead. Defaults to 1.

flags.name: intro
flags.description: Tells MUGEN that the character is currently performing his intro pose. Must be asserted on every tick while the intro pose is being performed.

flags.name: invisible
flags.description: Turns the character invisible while asserted. Does not affect display of afterimages.

flags.name: roundnotover
flags.description: Tells MUGEN that the character is currently performing his win pose. Should be asserted on every tick while the win pose is being performed.

flags.name: nobardisplay
flags.description: Disables display of life, super bars, etc. while asserted.

flags.name: noBG
flags.description: Turns off the background. The screen is cleared to black.

flags.name: noFG
flags.description: Disables display of layer 1 of the stage (the foreground).

flags.name: nostandguard
flags.description: While asserted, disables standing guard for the character.

flags.name: nocrouchguard
flags.description: While asserted, disables crouching guard for the character.

flags.name: noairguard
flags.description: While asserted, disables air guard for the character.

flags.name: noautoturn
flags.description: While asserted, keeps the character from automatically turning to face the opponent.

flags.name: nojugglecheck
flags.description: While asserted, disables juggle checking. P2 can be juggled regardless of juggle points.

flags.name: nokosnd
flags.description: Suppresses playback of sound 11, 0 (the KO sound) for players who are knocked out. For players whose KO sound echoes, nokosnd must be asserted for 50 or more ticks after the player is KOed in order to suppress all echoes.

flags.name: nokoslow
flags.description: While asserted, keeps MUGEN from showing the end of the round in slow motion.

flags.name: noshadow
flags.description: While asserted, disables display of this player's shadows.

flags.name: globalnoshadow
flags.description: Disables display of all player, helper and explod shadows.

flags.name: nomusic
flags.description: While asserted, pauses playback of background music.

flags.name: nowalk
flags.description: While asserted, the player cannot enter his walk states, even if he has control. Use to prevent run states from canceling into walking.

flags.name: timerfreeze
flags.description: While asserted, keeps the round timer from counting down. Useful to keep the round from timing over in the middle of a splash screen.

flags.name: unguardable
flags.description: While asserted, all the asserting player's HitDefs become unblockable, i.e., their guardflags are ignored.

flags.name: AnimateHitpause
flags.description: While asserted, this flag makes the player's animation advance normally even during a hitpause.

flags.name: AnimFreeze
flags.description: While asserted, the player's animation will be frozen on the current frame.

flags.name: AutoGuard
flags.description: While asserted, makes the player guard automatically, without need to press back direction. The player will also switch automatically between standing and crouching guard.

flags.name: CameraFreeze
flags.description: While asserted, prevents the camera from updating, effectively freezing it in place.

flags.name: DrawUnder
flags.description: While asserted, makes the player sprites be drawn with the same properties of Explod `under` parameter. That is, if the player is on layer 0, it will always be drawn behind lifebars and character shadows.

flags.name: GlobalNoKo
flags.description: While asserted all players won't die from taking damage.

flags.name: NoAIButtonJam
flags.description: While asserted, disables the random direction and button jamming of Ikemen's default AI.

flags.name: NoAICheat
flags.description: While asserted, makes the player's AI unable to cheat commands, i.e. complete them without performing the respective inputs.

flags.name: NoAiLevel
flags.description: While asserted, makes the player AILevel and AILevelF triggers return 0.

flags.name: NoAirJump
flags.description: Disables the hard-coded state transitions to State 45 when `Ctrl=1 && StateType=A && Command="holdup"` and `AirJump.Num` allows

flags.name: NoBrake
flags.description: Disables the hard-coded state transitions to State 0 when `StateNo=20 && Command!="holdfwd" && Command!="holdback"`

flags.name: NoComboDisplay
flags.description: While asserted, disables displaying combo counter by this playerno (the flag has to be asserted on team leader to disable combo counter rendering for the teamside).

flags.name: NoCornerPush
flags.description: While asserted, the player won't be affected by HitDef `cornerpush.veloff`.

flags.name: NoCrouch
flags.description: Disables the hard-coded state transitions to State 10 when `Ctrl=1 && StateType=S && Command="holddown"`.

flags.name: NoDestroySelf
flags.description: While asserted, disables `destroyself` sctrl.

flags.name: NoDizzyPointsDamage
flags.description: While asserted, player won't be affected by a HitDef's dizzypoints parameter.

flags.name: NoFaceDisplay
flags.description: While asserted, disables displaying the face icon for this player.

flags.name: NoFaceP2
flags.description: While asserted, StateDef `facep2` parameter will have no effect.

flags.name: NoFastRecoverFromLieDown
flags.description: Disables the hard-coded faster recover from lie down on key input mashing when `StateType=L && GetHitVar(RecoverTime)>0`.

flags.name: NoFallCount
flags.description: Disables the hard-coded FallCount increment when `StateNo=5070 || StateNo=5100`.

flags.name: NoFallDefenceUp
flags.description: Disables the hard-coded defence increase when `StateNo=5070 || StateNo=5100`.

flags.name: NoFallHitflag
flags.description: While asserted, every `HitDef` will act as if its `HitFlag` has no `F` parameter. In other words, the player becomes unable to hit falling enemies.

flags.name: NoGetUpFromLieDown
flags.description: Disables the hard-coded state transitions to State 5120 when `StateNo=5110 && GetHitVar(RecoverTime)=0`.

flags.name: NoGuardKo
flags.description: While asserted player won't die from taking chip damage.

flags.name: NoGuardBarDisplay
flags.description: While asserted, disables displaying guardbars by this playerno.

flags.name: NoGuardDamage
flags.description: While asserted, player won't be affected by HitDef damage *guard_damage*.

flags.name: NoGuardPointsDamage
flags.description: While asserted, player won't be affected by HitDef guardpoints.

flags.name: NoHardcodedKeys
flags.description: Disables the hard-coded state transitions when pressing directional keys (combination of `NoJump`, `NoAirJump`, `NoCrouch`, `NoStand`, `NoWalk`, `NoBrake`, `NoStandGuard`, `NoCrouchGuard`, `NoAirGuard`).

flags.name: NoHitDamage
flags.description: While asserted, player won't be affected by HitDef damage *hit_damage*.

flags.name: NoInput
flags.description: While asserted, makes the player ignore any player/CPU inputs.

flags.name: NoIntroReset
flags.description: While asserted, prevents a player from being forced to their starting position after the round number announcement.

flags.name: NoJump
flags.description: Disables the hard-coded state transitions to State 40 when `Ctrl=1 && StateType=S && Command="holdup"`

flags.name: NoKo
flags.description:
While asserted, the player won't die from taking damage.

If `ikemenversion` is not 0, the `NoKO` flag affects only the player that called it. Otherwise, the MUGEN behavior is replicated, and all players are affected. The new `GlobalNoKo` flag can be used to replicate the old MUGEN behavior.

flags.name: NoKoFall
flags.description: While asserted, the player won't be forced to fall when receiving a hit that depletes their remaining life. In Mugen this was hardcoded into Training mode.

flags.name: NoKoVelocity
flags.description: While asserted, player won't be affected by HitDef velocity adjustments upon KO.

flags.name: NoLifeBarAction
flags.description: While asserted, disables displaying lifebar actions by this playerno (the flag has to be asserted on team leader to disable lifebar actions rendering for the teamside).

flags.name: NoLifeBarDisplay
flags.description: While asserted, disables displaying lifebars by this playerno.

flags.name: NoMakeDust
flags.description: While asserted, the player does not generate hardcoded dust effects. The `MakeDust` state controller will also have no effect.

flags.name: NoNameDisplay
flags.description: While asserted, disables displaying the Name by this playerno.

flags.name: NoPowerBarDisplay
flags.description: While asserted, disables displaying powerbars by this playerno (with team power share option enabled and/or lifebar design with only 1 powerbar per side, the flag has to be asserted on team leader to disable powerbar rendering for whole team).

flags.name: NoRedLifeDamage
flags.description: While asserted, player won't be affected by HitDef *redlife*.

flags.name: NoScore
flags.description: While asserted, player won't be affected by HitDef *score* or the `ScoreAdd` / `TargetScoreAdd` state controllers.

flags.name: NoStand
flags.description: Disables the hard-coded state transitions to State 12 when `StateType=C && Command!="holddown"`.

flags.name: NoStunBarDisplay
flags.description: While asserted, disables displaying stunbars by this playerno.

flags.name: NoTimeDisplay
flags.description: While asserted, disables displaying the fight screens `[Time]` elements.

flags.name: NoTurnTarget
flags.description: While asserted, keeps the opponent from automatically turning to face the player. This includes the `facep2` parameter.

flags.name: NoWinIconDisplay
flags.description: While asserted, disables displaying winicons by this playerno (the flag has to be asserted on team leader to disable winicon rendering for the teamside).

flags.name: PostRoundInput
flags.description: While asserted, player's inputs are not disabled post-match (`RoundState>2 || RoundState=-1`).

flags.name: ProjTypeCollision
flags.description: While asserted, the player will clash with projectiles (and other players with the same flag) if their `Clsn2` boxes overlap. This allows helpers to easily replicate this kind of projectile clashing.

flags.name: RoundFreeze
flags.description: While asserted, round related lifebar actions and internal timers are frozen (allows maintaining current roundstate).

flags.name: RoundNotSkip
flags.description: Disables intro and victory pose skipping via button press.

flags.name: RunFirst
flags.description: While asserted, makes the player code be processed before that of any other players.

flags.name: RunLast
flags.description: While asserted, makes the player code be processed after all other players.

flags.name: SizePushOnly
flags.description: In Ikemen, like Mugen, characters will push each other when both their size boxes (width * height) and their Clsn2 boxes overlap. Asserting this flag makes it so that only the size boxes are checked, as in most fighting games.

flags.name: SkipFightDisplay
flags.description: While asserted, the "fight" announcement on round start will be skipped.

flags.name: SkipKoDisplay
flags.description: While asserted, the KO announcement on round end will be skipped.

flags.name: SkipRoundDisplay
flags.description: While asserted, the round number announcement on round start will be skipped.

flags.name: SkipWinDisplay
flags.description: While asserted, the winner announcement on round end will be skipped.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = AssertSpecial
trigger1 = 1
flag = ...
flag2 = ...
flag3 = ...
flag4 = ...
flag5 = ...
flag6 = ...
flag7 = ...
flag8 = ...

sctrls.name: AttackDist
sctrls.description: Changes the value of the guard.dist parameter for the player's current HitDef. The guard.dist is the x-distance from P1 in which P2 will go into a guard state if P2 is holding the direction away from P1. The effect of guard.dist only takes effect when P1 has `movetype = A`.

params.changeNote: The `value` parameter now takes a second number. This number sets the distance that a player can attack behind the enemy and still allow them to enter proximity guard.
params.name: value
params.description: New guard distance, in pixels.

params.name: Width
params.description: Works the same as Value.

params.name: Height
params.description: Changes the value of the attack.dist.height parameter for the player's current HitDef.

params.name: Depth
params.description: Changes the value of the attack.dist.depth parameter for the player's current HitDef.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = AttackDist
trigger1 = 1
value = 100, 50

sctrls.name: AttackMulSet
sctrls.description: Sets the player's attack multiplier. All damage the player gives is scaled by this amount.

params.changeNote: Sets the attack multiplier for all types of damage.
params.name: value
params.description: Specifies the desired multiplier. For instance, an *attack_mul* of 2 deals double damage.

params.name: Damage
params.description: Sets an attack multiplier for regular damage only.

params.name: DizzyPoints
params.description: Sets an attack multiplier for dizzy points only.

params.name: GuardPoints
params.description: Sets an attack multiplier for guard points only.

params.name: RedLife
params.description: Sets an attack multiplier for red life only.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = AttackMulSet
trigger1 = 1
Damage = 0.50
RedLife = 2.00
DizzyPoints = 0.75
GuardPoints = 0.00

sctrls.name: BGPalFX
sctrls.description: Same as PalFX, except that this affects the palette of the background and lifebars instead of the palette of the character. See the PalFX section for details on the parameters to BGPalFX.
changeNotes: BGPalFX now also accepts `ID` and `index` parameters. This allows it to apply PalFX to specific BG elements of the stage.

params.name: ID
params.description: The ID of the stage BG element to affect. Defaults to -1 (any).

params.name: Index
params.description: The index of the stage BG element to affect. Defaults to -1 (any).

sctrls.example:
[State Test]; Invert colors for the sixth BG element with any ID
type = BGPalFX
trigger1 = 1
ID = -1
index = 5
time = 10
invertall = 1

sctrls.name: BindToParent
sctrls.description: If the player is a helper, binds the player to a specified position relative to its parent. If the player is not a helper, this controller does nothing.

params.name: time
params.description: Specify number of ticks that this binding should be effective. Defaults to 1.

params.name: facing
params.description: If *facing_flag* is -1, makes the player always face the opposite direction from its parent during the binding time. If *facing_flag* is 1, makes the player always face the same direction as its parent during the binding time. If *facing_flag* is 0, the player will not turn regardless of what its parent does. Defaults to 0.

params.name: pos
params.description: *pos_x* and *pos_y* specify the offsets (from the parent's axis) to bind to. Defaults to `0, 0`.

sctrls.name: BindToRoot
sctrls.description: If the player is a helper, binds the player to a specified position relative to its root. If the player is not a helper, this controller does nothing.

params.name: time
params.description: Specify number of ticks that this binding should be effective. Defaults to 1.

params.name: facing
params.description: If *facing_flag* is -1, makes the player always face the opposite direction from its root during the binding time. If *facing_flag* is 1, makes the player always face the same direction as its root during the binding time. If *facing_flag* is 0, the player will not turn regardless of what its root does. Defaults to 0.

params.name: pos
params.description: *pos_x* and *pos_y* specify the offsets (from the root's axis) to bind to. Defaults to `0, 0`.

sctrls.name: BindToTarget
sctrls.description: Binds the player to a specified position relative to the specified target.

params.name: time
params.description: Specify number of ticks that this binding should be effective. Defaults to 1.

params.name: ID
params.description: Specifies ID number of the target to bind to. Defaults to -1 (pick any target).

params.name: pos
params.description: *pos_x* and *pos_y* specify the offsets (from the bind point) to bind to. The bind point defaults to the target's axis. If *postype* is `Foot`, then the bind point is the target's axis. If *postype* is `Mid`, then the bind point is the target's midsection. If *postype* is `Head`, then the bind point is the target's head. In the latter two cases, the bind point is determined from the values of the head.pos and mid.pos parameters in the target's CNS file. The bind point is not guaranteed to match up with the target's head or midsection.

params.name: PosZ
params.description: Specify the offset (in the z-axis) to bind to. Can be skipped, so it's backward compatible with lines having only x,y declared.

params.name: Index
params.description: The index of the target to bind to. Defaults to 0 (first one).

sctrls.name: Camera
sctrls.description:
**This SCTRL is still experimental and subject to possible changes, there is no guarantee this will be supported as is in future IKEMEN Go versions.**

Changes the camera position and the way players interact with screen and stage edges.

params.name: view
params.description: Specifies the type of view to implement. Valid values are "Fighting", "Follow" or "Free". Fighting works like common MUGEN camera. Follow anchors the camera to a specific player/helper and follows it. Free is not bound to anything other than the own camera's limitations.

sctrls.name: ChangeAnim
sctrls.description: Changes the action number of the player's animation.

params.name: value
params.description: *anim_no* is the action number to change to.

params.name: elem
params.description: *elem_no* is the element number within the specified action to start from.

params.name: ElemTime
params.description: Specifies the exact time of an animation element to change to. Defaults to 0.

params.name: AnimPlayerNo
params.description: This parameter lets a character use the specified animation from another character. Defaults to own playerno.

params.name: SpritePlayerNo
params.description: This parameter lets a character use the specified sprites from another character. Defaults to own playerno.

params.name: ReadPlayerID
params.description: This parameter lets a character use the specified animation from another character, including their sprites.

sctrls.example:
[State 1000, Anim]; Change to animation 1003, element 4, second frame
type = ChangeAnim
trigger1 = Time = 30
value = 1003
elem = 4
elemtime = 1

sctrls.name: ChangeAnim2
sctrls.description: Like ChangeAnim, except this controller should be used if you have placed P2 in a custom state via a hit and wish to change P2's animation to one specified in P1's air file. For example, when making throws, use this to change P2 to a being-thrown animation.

params.name: ElemTime
params.description: See ChangeAnim.

params.name: ReadPlayerID
params.description: This parameter lets a character use the specified animation from another character, but maintaining their own sprites.

sctrls.name: ChangeMovelist
sctrls.description: Selects which movelist assigned in the character's DEF file should be displayed in the Pause menu command list.

params.name: value
params.description:
Specifies the index of the movelist to use. Defaults to 0.

The movelist files are specified in the character's DEF file, under the `[Files]` group. `movelist` and `movelist0` both refer to index 0.

sctrls.example:
[State 5900, Evil Ryu movelist]
type = ChangeMovelist
trigger1 = PalNo > 6
value = 1

sctrls.name: ChangeState
sctrls.description: Changes the state number of the player.

params.name: value
params.description: *state_no* is the number of the state to change to.

params.name: ctrl
params.description: *ctrl_flag* is the value to set the player's control flag to. 0 for no control, nonzero for control.

params.name: anim
params.description: This is the action number to switch to. If omitted, the player's animation will remain unchanged.

params.name: Continue
params.description: Due to the way State -1 is normally used to read inputs and change states, Mugen had it so that using a `ChangeState` in a negative state would stop the execution of the rest of the code in that state. Setting `Continue` to 1 will disable this behavior. When a `ChangeState` is redirected, `Continue` will default to 1.

sctrls.example:
; Change to standing state, and give player control  
type = ChangeState  
value = 0  
ctrl = 1

sctrls.name: ClearClipboard
sctrls.description: Erases any text currently on the player's clipboard.

sctrls.name: CtrlSet
sctrls.description: Sets the player's control flag.

params.name: value
params.description: Set to nonzero to have control, or 0 to disable control.

sctrls.name: DefenceMulSet
sctrls.description: Sets the player's defense multiplier. All damage the player takes is scaled by this amount.
changeNotes:
In Mugen, `DefenceMulSet` changes the player's final defense multiplier. That means it will override any defense buffs such as those gained through the `fall.defence_up` constant or the `SuperPause` `p2defmul` parameter. In Ikemen GO, it is only another multiplier, meaning the other defense buffs will still work correctly.

Characters with `ikemenversion` will have `DefenceMulSet` work correctly and more intuitively by default. See `MulType` and `OnHit`.

params.name: value
params.description: Specifies the defense multiplier.

params.name: MulType
params.description:
Defines how damage taken should be multiplied.

If 0, damage taken is multiplied by `value`. If 1, defense is multiplied by `value` (therefore the damage is divided).

Defaults to 1 for characters with `ikemenversion`, and to 0 otherwise.

params.name: OnHit
params.description:
Defines if the defense value should also apply outside of `moveType = H`.

If 0, the defense value works without delay. If 1, the defense value is only active if the char is already in `moveType = H`.

Defaults to 0 for characters with `ikemenversion`, and 1 otherwise.

sctrls.example:
; All damage the player takes is reduced to half.  
type = DefenceMulSet  
value = 0.5

sctrls.name: Depth
sctrls.description: Temporarily changes the depth size of the player's for 1 frame. Similar to Width in function.

params.name: edge
params.description: Sets the player's edge depth in front and behind. Edge depth determines how close the player can get to the topbound and botbound of the screen. These parameters default to 0,0 if omitted.

params.name: player
params.description: Sets the player depth in front and behind. Player depth determines how close the player can get to other players depth and also determines the hitable depth area of a player. These parameters default to 0,0 if omitted

params.name: value
params.description: This is a shorthand syntax for setting both edge depth and player depth simultaneously. This may only be used if the edge and player parameters are not specified.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = Depth
trigger1 = P2StateType = A
value = 0, 0
player = 40, 0
edge = 0, 0

sctrls.name: DepthBound
sctrls.description: Lets a character bypass topbound and botbound from stage.

params.name: value
params.description: If bound_flag is 0, the player will be allowed to move off the z boundaries. If 1, the player is constrained within the zboundaries. Defaults to 0 if omitted.

params.name: movecamera
params.description: If 1, specifies that camera should pan to follow the player in the z direction. Defaults to 0 if omitted.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = DepthBound
trigger1 = StateType = H
value = 1
movecamera = 0

sctrls.name: DestroySelf
sctrls.description: If called by a helper-type character, DestroySelf causes that character to be removed from the field of play. DestroySelf is not valid for non-helper characters.

params.name: recursive
params.description: If 1, all helper descendents of this helper will also be destroyed. Defaults to 0.

params.name: removeexplods
params.description: If 1, all explods belonging to the helper will also be removed. If *recursive_flag* is 1, explods belonging to descendents of the helper will also be removed. Defaults to 0.

sctrls.name: Dialogue
sctrls.description: Assigns dialogue data to be displayed either right before the lifebar calls the fight during first round (last frame of  RoundState = 1) or at the last active frame of the final round (RoundState = 4, right before screen starts fading out). If more than 1 player calls this sctrl, who will end up initiating dialogue is chosen randomly.

params.name: textX
params.description: String containing information needed for displaying dialogue. There can be multiple *text* parameters assigned, each suffixed with numbers in ascending order. The parameter stores both text, as well as optional tokens (enclosed in <> brackets) for controlling other aspects of dialogue (listed below).

params.name: hidebars
params.description: Set to nonzero to hide lifebars as soon as the sctrl is called (by default lifebar is hidden only when actual dialogue starts).

params.name: force
params.description:
Set to nonzero to force dialogue start immediately, ignoring normal rules.

How the rendered dialogue will look like (positioning, default face sprites, background definition, default time between text etc.) is controlled by `[Dialogue Info]` screenpack parameters (refer to system.def distributed with engine for a working example). By default player who called the state controller will use screenpack parameters prefixed with *p1* and his *enemy(0)* will be assigned to use *p2* parameters (this is adjustable via text tokens).

With appropriate screenpack parameters it's possible to skip to the next *text* parameter during dialogue via button press, without ending it all together. If this…

sctrls.example:
[State 191, Dialogue]
type = Dialogue
trigger1 = enemy,Name="Demitri Maximoff"
hidebars = 1
text1 = "<p1><p1face=self,9100,0><p2face=enemy,9100,4><sound=self,9100,0>Die monster.<wait=60> You don't belong in this world!"
text2 = "<p2><sound=enemy,9100,0>It was not by my hand that I am once again given flesh.<wait=120> I was called here by humans, who wish to pay me tribute.<wait=170>"
text3 = "<p1><p1face=self,9100,1><sound=self,9100,1>Tribute!?!<wait=30> You steal men's souls, and make them your slaves!<wait=90>"
text4 = "<p2><p2face=enemy,9100,2><sound=enemy,9100,1>Perhaps the same could be said of all religions...<wait=30>"
text5 = "<p1><p1face=self,9100,7><sound=self,9100,2>Your words are as empty as your soul!<wait=80><p1face=self,9100,4> Mankind ill needs a savior such as you!<wait=70>"
text6 = "<p2><p2face=enemy,9100,5><sound=enemy,9100,2>What is a man?<wait=75><p1face=self,9100,2> A miserable little pile of secrets!<wait=75> But enough talk...<wait=30> Have at you!"

[State 180, Dialogue]
type = Dialogue
trigger1 = Win && enemy,Name="Demitri Maximoff"
text1 = "<p2><p1face=self,9100,6><p2face=enemy,9100,3><sound=enemy,9200,0><anim=self,0><state=enemy,5500>How?<wait=120> How is that I have been so defeated?<wait=120>"
text2 = "<p1><p1face=self,9100,3><sound=self,9200,0><displayname=enemy>, you have been doomed ever since you lost the ability to love.<wait=20>"
text3 = "<p2><p2face=enemy,9100,0><sound=enemy,9200,1>Ah...<wait=90> sarcasm.<p1face=self,9100,5><wait=40><state=self,186>"

sctrls.name: DisplayToClipboard
sctrls.description: This controller is only useful for debugging. DisplayToClipboard clears the player clipboard and prints a specified message to it. Display of the player clipboards is enabled in debug mode (press Ctrl+D).
changeNotes: Unlike Mugen, Ikemen GO can use unlimited amount of numeric arguments. Also it supports format specifiers, e.g. %0.2f (prints float value truncated to 2 digits), %v (prints the value in a default format and optimal formatting, regardless if it's int, float or string).

params.name: text
params.description:
format_string must be encased in double-quotes. It is a printf format string, so if you know about printf, you can skip this description. The format string contains any text you wish to display. You can also use \n to generate a line break, and \t to generate a tab character (tab width is equivalent to 4 characters). To display the value of an arithmetic expression, you can put a %d (for ints) or a %f (for floats) in the format string, then specify the expression in the params list. To display a % character, you must put %% in the format string.

Only signed integer and floating-point format specifiers are accepted: %d, %i, %f, %F, %e, %E, %g, or %G. Length-modified format specifiers (e.g.,…

params.name: params
params.placeholder: exp_1, exp_2, exp_3, exp_4, exp_5, exp_6
params.description:
Up to 6 numeric arguments can be specified in the format string. These should be listed under the params item, in order. The type of each parameter must match its format specifier. You cannot specify more or less parameters than are called for in the format string.

If there is a type mismatch between the format specifier and the parameter actually provided, then the actual value of the parameter will be shown in an appropriate form for that type, using default formatting options.

sctrls.example:
type = DisplayToClipboard  
text=`The value of var(17) is %d, which is %f%% of 23.\n\t--Kiwi.`  
params = var(17):=1,var(17)/.230  
  
Displays the following to the player's clipboard:  
  
The value of var(17) is 1, which is 4.347826% of 23.  
    --Kiwi.

sctrls.name: DizzyPointsAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the specified amount to the player's dizzy points.

params.name: value
params.description: *add_amt* is the number to add to the player's dizzy points.

sctrls.example: dizzyPointsAdd{value: 10}

sctrls.name: DizzyPointsSet
sctrls.description: Sets the amount of dizzy points that the player has.

params.name: value
params.description: *set_amt* is the new value to set the player's dizzy points to.

sctrls.example: dizzyPointsSet{value: 100}

sctrls.name: DizzySet
sctrls.description: Sets the player's Dizzy flag. For the duration that this flag is set, combo hit counter does not reset and the combo count lifebar text will stay on screen.

params.name: value
params.description: Set to nonzero to add Dizzy flag, or 0 to remove it.

sctrls.example: dizzySet{value: 1}

sctrls.name: EnvColor
sctrls.description: Turns the whole screen a solid color, excepting foreground-layer animations like hit sparks and `ontop` explods. Foreground layers of the stage will not be visible.

params.name: value
params.description: Specifies the R, G, and B components of the color to set the screen to. Each component should be an integer between 0 and 255. The larger a component, the more of that color will appear in the environment color. The default is 255,255,255 (pure white).

params.name: time
params.description: Specifies how many ticks the environment color should be displayed. Defaults to 1 tick. Set to -1 to have the EnvColor persist indefinitely.

params.name: under
params.description: Set *under_flag* to 1 to have the environment color drawn under characters and projectiles. In other words, characters and projectiles will be visible on top of the colored backdrop. Defaults to 0.

sctrls.name: EnvShake
sctrls.description: Causes the screen to shake vertically.

params.name: time
params.description: Specifies the number of ticks to shake the screen for.

params.name: freq
params.description: *shake_speed* is a float between 0 (slow shake) to 180 (fast shake). Defaults to 60.

params.name: ampl
params.description: The larger the amplitude, the farther the screen shakes up and down. A negative amplitude means that the screen will shake down first. Defaults to -4 in 240p, -8 in 480p, -16 in 720p.

params.name: phase
params.description: Specifies the phase offset for the shaking. The default is 0, unless the frequency multiplier is 90 or greater. In this case, the default phase offset is 90.

params.name: Decay
params.description:
Applies an exponential decay to the shake amplitude over time, making it fade out automatically.

- `decay = 0`: no fading
- `0 < decay < 1`: fades slow, then fast
- `decay = 1`: fades linearly
- `decay > 1`: fades fast, then slow

params.name: Dir
params.description: Changes the direction in degrees in which the shake is applied. Defaults to 0. For a negative amplitude, 90 will make the screen shake from left to right.

params.name: DirAdd
params.description: Increases the shaking angle by the specified value each frame. Allows the effect to appear more exaggerated and erratic.

params.name: Mul
params.description: For every EnvShake cycle, the amplitude is multiplied by this value. Defaults to 1. Cycle duration is determined by frequency, with a frequency of 180 needing two frames to complete one cycle.

sctrls.example:
[State Shake]
type = envshake
trigger1 = !time
time = 30
ampl = 10
freq = 90
decay = 1.5

sctrls.name: Explod
sctrls.description: The Explod controller is a flexible tool for displaying animations such as sparks, dust and other visual effects. Its functionality includes that of GameMakeAnim, which is now deprecated.

params.name: anim
params.description: *anim_no* specifies the number of the animation to play back. The 'F' prefix is optional: if included, then the animation is played back from fightfx.air.

params.name: ID
params.description: *id_no* specifies an ID number for this explod. Used to identify particular explods in triggers and controllers that affect explods.

params.name: space
params.description:
Specifies the coordinate space in which the explod is to be created. Valid values for *space* are:

**screen**

This coordinate space maps to the screen. The upper-left corner is `0, 0` and the lower-right corner is `ScreenWidth, ScreenHeight` (refer to the triggers with these names). Explods created in screen space are not affected by camera movement or zoom.

**stage**

This coordinate space maps to the stage space in which players reside. `0, 0` is the center of the stage at ground level. Explods created in screen space are affected by camera movement and zoom. This is the default.

params.name: pos
params.description: If the explod is not bound, *off_x* and *off_y* specify the position at which to create the explod. If the explod is bound, *off_x* and *off_y* specify the offset from the object to which the explod is bound to.

params.name: facing
params.description: Set *facing* to 1 to have the explod face in the same direction as the positive *off_x*, and -1 to have the explod face in the opposite direction. Defaults to 1.

params.name: vfacing
params.description: Set *vfacing* to -1 to have the explod display vertically flipped, or 1 to have the explod display vertically unflipped. Defaults to 1.

params.name: bindID
params.description: ID number of a player or helper to bind to. The position of a bound explod is relative to the object that it is bound to. Special values are -1 (bind to any single player) and -2 (do not bind). Defaults to -2.  The bindtime parameter is required if bindID is not -2. Screen space explods cannot be bound.

params.name: bindtime
params.description: Specifies the number of game ticks to keep the explod bound. After the bindtime has expired, the explod will be explod will no longer be bound to the bind point, and will maintain its position (unless affected by the vel or accel parameters). If *bind_time* is -1, then the explod will be bound until the explod is removed or another controller affects the bindtime.

params.name: vel
params.description: Specifies initial X and Y velocity components for the explod. These are interpreted relative to the explod's `facing` direction. These default to 0 if omitted.

params.name: accel
params.description: Specifies X and Y acceleration components for the explod. These default to 0.

params.name: removetime
params.description: If *rem_time* is positive, the explod will be removed after having been displayed for that number of game ticks. If *rem_time* is -1, the explod will be displayed indefinitely. If *rem_time* is -2, the explod will be removed when its animtime reaches 0. The default value is -2.

params.name: supermovetime
params.description: Specifies the number of ticks that the explod will be unfrozen during a SuperPause. Used where you want the explod to be animated during a SuperPause, such as for custom super sparks. Defaults to 0.

params.name: pausemovetime
params.description: Specifies the number of ticks that the explod should be unfrozen during a Pause. Defaults to 0.

params.name: scale
params.description: *x_scale* and *y_scale* specify the scaling factors to apply to the explod in the horizontal and vertical directions. Both default to 1 (no scaling) if omitted.

params.name: angle
params.description: *angle* specifies the explod's drawing angle in degrees. Defaults to 0.

params.name: yangle
params.description: *y_angle* specifies the explod's drawing angle around the y-axis in degrees. Defaults to 0.

params.name: xangle
params.description: *x_angle* specifies the explod's drawing angle around the x-axis in degrees. Defaults to 0.

params.name: sprpriority
params.description: *pr* specifies the drawing priority for the explod. Animations with higher priority get drawn over animations with lesser priority. For instance, setting `sprpriority = -3` will cause the explod to be drawn under most characters and other explods, which usually have `sprpriority >= -2`. Defaults to 0 if omitted.

params.name: ontop
params.description: Set `ontop = 1` to have the explod drawn over all other sprites and background layers. This parameter has precedence over sprpriority. Defaults to 0.

params.name: shadow
params.description: If *shadow* is not 0, a shadow will be drawn for the explod, else no shadow will be drawn. Defaults to 0.

params.name: ownpal
params.description:
If *ownpal_flag* is 0, the explod color will be affected by subsequent execution of the player's PalFX and RemapPal controllers. This is normally the default.

If *ownpal_flag* is 1, the explod color will not be affected by subsequent execution of the player's PalFX and RemapPal controllers. This is the default if the anim is from fightfx.air.

params.name: remappal
params.description: Forces a palette remap of the explod's indexed-color sprites to the specified palette. This parameter is used only if *ownpal_flag* is non-zero and a fight.def anim is not used. If *dst_pal_grp* is -1, this parameter will be ignored. Defaults to -1, 0.

params.name: removeongethit
params.description: Setting this to 1 will cause the explod removed if the player gets hit. Defaults to 0.

params.name: ignorehitpause
params.description: If this is 1, the explod will be animated independently of the player that created it. If set to 0, it will not be updated when the player is in hitpause. Defaults to 1.

params.name: trans
params.description: Overrides the explod's animation transparency settings. See the Trans controller for details. An `alpha` parameter may be specified if trans_type is an additive type. If omitted, does nothing.

params.name: postype
params.description:
*postype_string* specifies how to interpret the pos parameters. In all cases, a positive *off_y* means a downward displacement.

Valid values for *postype_string* are the following:

**p1**

Interprets pos relative to p1's axis. A positive *off_x* is toward the front of p1. This is the default value for postype for characters with a `mugenversion` of 1.0 or less.

**p2**

Interprets pos relative to p2's axis. A positive *off_x* is toward the front of p2.

**front**

Interprets *off_x* relative to the edge of the screen that p1 is facing toward, and *off_y* relative to the top of the screen. A positive *off_x* is to the right of the screen, whereas a negative *off_x* is toward the…

params.name: random
params.description: Causes the explod's bind point to be displaced by a random amount when created. *rand_x* specifies the displacement range in the x direction, and *rand_y* specifies the displacement range in the y direction. For instance, if pos = 0, 0 and random = 40,80, then the explod's x location will be a random number between -20 and 19, and its y location will be a random number between -40 and 39. Both arg1 and arg2 default to 0 if omitted.

params.name: supermove
params.description: *This parameter is deprecated; use supermovetime parameter instead.* Set supermove = 1 to have the explod persist until the end of a super pause, regardless of the value of removetime. Defaults to 0.

params.name: AfterImage
params.description: Explods now support AfterImage parameters (e.g. afterimage.time, afterimage.length, afterimage.trans). Usage is identical to Projectile's AfterImage.

params.name: AnimElem
params.description: Sets the element where the explod's animation should start. Defaults to 1.

params.name: AnimPlayerNo
params.description: This parameter lets a explod use the specified animation from another character. Defaults to own playerno.

params.name: HideWithBars
params.description: This parameter hides the explod automatically when the fight screen is hidden. Defaults to 0.

params.name: SpritePlayerNo
params.description:
This parameter lets a explod use the specified sprites from another character. Defaults to own playerno.

This parameter lets a explod use the specified sprites from another character. Defaults to own playerno.

params.name: AnimElemTime
params.description: Sets the time at which the explod's animation element should start. Defaults to 0.

params.name: AnimFreeze
params.description: Freezes the explod's animation. Defaults to 0.

params.name: FocalLength
params.description: Focal Length of the projection. Does nothing when `projection` is not perspective or perspective2. This value is fixed in Mugen 1.1, the explods will look differently under different different resolution/loaclcoord/camera zoom. In Ikemen, this value scales internally like xy scales so that the explods will always look the same. Default value is 2048.

params.name: Friction
params.description: Applies friction to explod on the defined axis (Friction value example: 0.95).

params.name: interpolation.time
params.description: Specifies the time period of the animation (if omitted, defaults to 0).

params.name: interpolation.animelem
params.description: Specifies the target animelem for the interpolation. If animelem is omitted, defaults to 1. animfreeze will stop the animation from going further than interpolation.animelem.

params.name: interpolation.alpha
params.description: Specifies the source and destination alpha values for the interpolation. sub and add1 are not supported.

params.name: interpolation.angle
params.description:
Specifies the target angle, xangle, and yangle values for the interpolation.

Note: For the nightly build, these have been separated into individual parameters.

params.name: interpolation.offset
params.description: Specifies the target x and y offset values for the interpolation.

params.name: interpolation.scale
params.description: Specifies the target x and y scale values for the interpolation.

params.name: interpolation.xshear
params.description: Specifies the target xshear value.

params.name: interpolation.focallength
params.description:
Specifies the target focallength value.

PalFX is also compatible with the syntax. **interpolation.palfx.time** and **ownppal = 1** are required for any of the parameters to work.

params.name: interpolation.palfx.mul
params.description: Specifies the target red, green, and blue multiplication values. If palfx.mul is omitted, defaults to 256, 256, 256.

params.name: interpolation.palfx.add
params.description: Specifies the target red, green, and blue addition values. If palfx.add is omitted, defaults to 0, 0, 0.

params.name: interpolation.palfx.hue
params.description: Specifies the target hue value. If palfx.hue is omitted, defaults to 0.

params.name: interpolation.palfx.color
params.description:
Specifies the target color value. If palfx.color is omitted, defaults to 256.

These parameters can be used interchangeably.

params.name: LayerNo
params.description: Specify on which layer the explod should be drawn. Valid values are -1, 0 and 1. Defaults to the same layer as the player. Layer number 1 is effectively the same as the legacy `ontop` parameter.

params.name: PalFx
params.description: Apply palette effects on explods. The parameters are the same as in the HitDef controller. Requires `ownpal` to be a nonzero value.

params.name: Projection
params.description:
Affect how the explod is drawn when `xangle` or `yangle` is not zero.
- orthographic: The default value when Mugen version is not 1.1 or Ikemen version is not 0. The explod is drawn using orthographic projection.
- perspective: The default value when Mugen version is 1.1 and Ikemen version is 0. The explod is drawn using perspective projection. Distortion is affected by the position of the sprite relative to the center of the screen.
- perspective2: The explod is drawn using perspective projection. Distortion is affected by the position of the sprite relative to the center of the animation.

params.name: Reflection
params.description: If 0, disables reflection on the explod regardless of its shadow color. If 1, enables reflection on the explod regardless of its shadow color. Defaults to showing a reflection if the explod's shadow is not 0, 0, 0.

params.name: RemoveOnChangeState
params.description: If set to 1, the Explod will be removed if the character changes state. Defaults to 0.

params.name: Shader
params.description:
Specifying the name of the currently loaded custom shader will apply that shader to Explod.

Note: In the nightly build the syntax changed to `shader.name`.

params.name: ShaderTime
params.description:
Specifying this parameter will remove the custom shader after it has been displayed for the specified number of ticks. The default value is -1.

Note: In the nightly build the syntax changed to `shader.time`.

params.name: ShaderParam.pX
params.description:
Specifies the value to send to the custom shader. The value specified here can be used as a variable within the custom shader. X is limited to 0 to 15, and a maximum of 16 values ​​can be sent.

Note: In the nightly build the syntax changed to `shader.paramX`.

params.name: ShaderTexX.spr
params.description: Note: In the nightly build the syntax changed to `shader.texX.spr`.

params.name: ShaderTexX.anim
params.description:
Specifies the texture to send to the custom shader. The sprites specified here can be used as textures within the custom shader. You can specify 1 or 2 for X, and send up to two sprites. Each tex can be assigned either a sprite number (spr) or an anim number. It is not possible to assign both sprite and anim numbers to the same tex number simultaneously. Note that since textures are loaded as raw data, images with palettes may not display correctly as is.

Note: In the nightly build the syntax changed to `shader.texX.anim`.

params.name: shader.playerno
params.description: Specifies the player number who owns the shader to be used. Defaults to own player number.

params.name: shader.shadow
params.description: Specifies if the explod shadow is affected by the shader. Defaults to 1.

params.name: shader.reflection
params.description: Specifies if the explod reflection is affected by the shader. Defaults to 1.

params.name: shader.afterimage
params.description: Specifies if the explod afterimage is affected by the shader. Defaults to 1.

params.name: syncid
params.description: Specifies the ID of a character to synchronize with. The Explod will group with the target in the draw order. If syncparams is 1, it also copies the target's drawing properties (Position, Scale, Angle, Trans, etc.).

params.name: synclayer
params.description:
Adjusts the drawing order relative to the character specified in syncid.
* 0: Same layer as the character (default).
* \> 0: Drawn in front of the character.
* < 0: Drawn behind the character.

params.name: syncparams
params.description: If set to 1, visual parameters (Scale, Angle, Trans, etc.) are continuously copied from the character specified in syncid. If set to 0, only the draw order is synchronized. Defaults to 1.

params.name: under
params.description: If set to 1 and the explod is on layer 0, it will always be drawn behind lifebars and character shadows.

params.name: window
params.description: This parameter takes four numbers (similar to the format of a Clsn box) which forms a rectangle outside of which the pixels will not be rendered.

params.name: xshear
params.description: Specifies the amount of horizontal shearing to apply to the explod. Defaults to 0.

sctrls.example:
[State 0, Custom Afterimage]
type = Explod
trigger1 = time%5=0
anim = anim
animelem = animelemno(0)
animfreeze = 1
ID = 1000
postype = none
pos = pos x+camerapos x,pos y
facing = 1
vfacing = 1
bindtime = 1
supermovetime = 0
pausemovetime = 0
scale = 1,1
sprpriority = 10
ontop = 0
shadow = 0,0,0
ownpal = 1
trans = add
removetime = 40
palfx.time = 40
palfx.sinmul = -255,-255,-255,160
removeongethit = 0
ignorehitpause = 1

sctrls.name: ExplodBindTime
sctrls.description: Changes the position binding time of the player's explods.

params.name: ID
params.description: Only explods with ID number equal to *id_no* will have their position binding affected. Set ID to -1 to affect the binding of all explods. The default value is -1.

params.name: time
params.description: Specifies the number of ticks for which the explods should be bound to their binding points (defined at the time the explods were created). A time of -1 binds the explods indefinitely or until another controller changes the bindtime. Defaults to 1 tick.

sctrls.name: FallEnvShake
sctrls.description: Shakes the screen using the fall.envshake parameters set by an attack (see HitDef controller). This controller is effective only if GetHitVar(fall.envshake.time) is not zero, and it sets GetHitVar(fall.envshake.time) to zero after being executed. This controller is used in common1.cns to shake the screen when a player falls, and is not normally useful otherwise.

sctrls.name: ForceFeedback
sctrls.description: Creates force feedback for supported force feedback devices. This controller is not implemented in MUGEN 1.0. Parameters to the ForceFeedback controller may not be specified using arithmetic expressions. It is an exception in this regard.
changeNotes: Note: The below parameters are considered "new API" and override all `freq` and `ampl` parameters of ForceFeedback. `ampl` is ignored regardless of API used.

params.name: waveform
params.description: Valid waveforms are `sine`, `square`, `sinesquare`, and `off`. For the Dual Shock controller, a sine waveform corresponds to the large rumble motor, and a square waveform corresponds to the smaller buzzer motor. sinesquare, of course, corresponds to both motors simultaneously. Use `off` to turn off any force feedback that is currently executing. waveform defaults to sine.

params.name: time
params.description: Specifies how long the force feedback should last, in ticks. Defaults to 60.

params.name: freq
params.description: Force feedback frequency varies between 0 and 255. The formula used to determine force feedback frequency is `start + *d1* * t + *d2* * t ** 2 + *d3* * t ** 3` where t represents the number of ticks elapsed since the force feedback was initiated. Defaults to `freq = 128, 0, 0, 0`. Currently, the frequency parameter is completely ignored.

params.name: ampl
params.description: Force feedback amplitude varies between 0 and 255. The formula used to determine force feedback frequency is `start + *d1* * t + *d2* * t ** 2 + *d3* * t ** 3`, where t represents the number of ticks elapsed since the force feedback was initiated. Defaults to `ampl = 128,0, 0, 0`

params.name: self
params.description: If *self_flag* is 1, then P1's pad will vibrate. If self is 0, then P2's pad will vibrate. Defaults to 1.

params.name: lo
params.description: Sets the frequency for the low frequency (left) rumble motor. Defaults to 0.

params.name: hi
params.description: Sets the frequency for the high frequency (right) rumble motor. Defaults to 0.

sctrls.name: GameMakeAnim
sctrls.description: Creates a game animation, like a hit spark or a super charging effect. This controller has been superseded by Explod and is now considered deprecated. Support for it may be removed in future versions.

params.name: value
params.description: Specifies the animation number (from fightfx) of the animation to play. Defaults to 0.

params.name: under
params.description: If *under_flag* is 1, the animation is drawn behind the character sprites. Defaults to 0 (draw over characters).

params.name: pos
params.description: Specifies the position to display the animation at, relative to the player axis. Defaults to `0, 0`.

params.name: random
params.description: The position of the animation will be displaced in the x and y directions by (different) random amounts. The displacement can be as large as half of rand_amt. Defaults to 0.

sctrls.name: GetHitVarSet
sctrls.description: Changes a player's `GetHitVar` directly, without requiring a hit.
sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = GetHitVarSet
trigger1 = time = 10
fall.recovertime= 0

sctrls.name: Gravity
sctrls.description: Accelerates the player downwards, using the value of the player's `yaccel` constant.
sctrls.example:
; Applies constant acceleration throughout state  
trigger1 = 1  
type = Gravity

sctrls.name: GroundLevelOffset
sctrls.description: Applies a temporary offset to the player's ground level, which is otherwise 0. This makes the player treat a different position as `pos y = 0`, and therefore allows coding features such as platforms.
sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = GroundLevelOffset
trigger1 = Pos X + CameraPos X = [-160, 0]
trigger1 = Pos Y + GroundLevel <= -60
value = -60

sctrls.name: GuardBreakSet
sctrls.description: Sets the player's Guard Break flag.

params.name: value
params.description: Set to nonzero to add Guard Break flag, or 0 to remove it.

sctrls.example: guardBreakSet{value: 1}

sctrls.name: GuardPointsAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the specified amount to the player's guard points.

params.name: value
params.description: *add_amt* is the number to add to the player's guard points.

sctrls.example: guardPointsAdd{value: 10}

sctrls.name: GuardPointsSet
sctrls.description: Sets the amount of guard points that the player has.

params.name: value
params.description: *set_amt* is the new value to set the player's guard points to.

sctrls.example: guardPointsSet{value: 100}

sctrls.name: Height
sctrls.description: Temporarily changes the vertical size of the player's "push box" for 1 frame. Similar to Width in function: the values are added to the height, as defined in the player's constants file—they do not override them. A positive value will make the box larger, and a negative one will make it smaller.
sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = Height
trigger1 = P2StateType = L
value = 0, -30

sctrls.name: Helper
sctrls.description: Creates another instance of the player as a helper character.

params.name: helpertype
params.description: ~~This parameter is deprecated; player-type helpers are not supported.~~ If helpertype = normal, then the helper will be allowed to move off the edge of the screen. Furthermore, the camera will not move to try to keep the helper on screen. If helpertype = player, then the helper will be constrained to the screen and will be followed by the camera, just like a normal player. Defaults to normal. If you plan to use a helper for camera manipulation, do not use a player-type helper; instead use the ScreenBound controller in a normal helper with the `movecamera` parameter.

params.changeNote: A helper's name can now use any string expression.
params.name: name
params.description: Specifies a name for this helper, which must be enclosed in double quotes. If omitted, the name defaults to `parent's helper`, where "parent" represents the name of the player creating the helper.

params.name: ID
params.description: Sets an ID number to refer to this helper by. Defaults to 0.

params.name: pos
params.description: Specifies the x and y offsets to create this helper at. The precise meaning of these parameters is dependent on the postype. Defaults to `0, 0`.

params.name: postype
params.description:
*postype_string* specifies the postype -- how to interpret the pos parameters. In all cases, a positive y offset means a downward displacement. In all cases, *off_y* is relative to the position of the player.

Valid values for *postype_string* are the following:

**p1**

Interprets offset relative to p1's axis. A positive *off_x* is toward the front of p1. This is the default value for postype.

**p2**

Interprets offset relative to p2's axis. A positive *off_x* is toward the front of p2. If p2 does not exist, the position is calculated with respect to p1 and a warning is logged.

**front**

Interprets *off_x* relative to the edge of the screen that p1 is facing toward. A positive *off_x*…

params.name: facing
params.description: If postype is left or right, setting *facing* to 1 will make the helper face the right, and a value of -1 makes the helper face left. For all other values of postype except p2, if *facing* is 1, the helper will face the same direction as the player. If *facing* is -1, the helper will face the opposite direction. In the case of postype = p2, *facing* has the same effect as above, except it is with respect to p2's facing. Defaults to 1.

params.name: stateno
params.description: Determines the state number that the helper starts off in. Defaults to 0.

params.changeNote: In Mugen this parameter accepts a single boolean int value that makes the helper being able to read command input and inherit its root's State -1. In Ikemen GO, on top of this functionality, the parameter optionally accepts more values that enable additional root's negative state inheritance (2 means that helper inherit its root's State -2 and so forth).
params.name: keyctrl
params.description: If *ctrl_flag* is 1, then the helper is able to read command input from the player (e.g., the keyboard or joystick). Also, the helper will inherit its root's State -1. If *ctrl_flag* is 0, then the helper does not have access to command input, and does not inherit State -1. The default value of *ctrl_flag* is 0.

params.name: ownpal
params.description:
If *ownpal_flag* is 0, the helper will be affected by subsequent execution of its parent's PalFX and RemapPal controllers. This is the default.

If *ownpal_flag* is 1, the helper will receive its own working palette which is independent of its parent's.

params.name: remappal
params.description: Forces a palette remap of the helper's indexed-color sprites to the specified palette. This parameter is used only if *ownpal_flag* is non-zero. If *dst_pal_grp* is -1, this parameter will be ignored. Defaults to -1, 0.

params.name: supermovetime
params.description: Specifies the number of ticks that the helper should be unfrozen during a SuperPause. Defaults to 0.

params.name: pausemovetime
params.description: Determines the number of ticks that the helper should be unfrozen during a Pause. Defaults to 0.

params.name: size.shadowoffset
params.description: These parameters have the same meaning as the corresponding parameters in the root's CNS file. You can specify one or more of these parameters to change it to a value suitable for this helper. Otherwise, they default to the values inherited from the parent.

params.name: ClsnProxy
params.description: If set to 1, any overlap with the helper's clsn boxes will instead affect its parent as if the helper's clsn boxes were part of the parent's anim. Defaults to 0.

params.name: ExtendsMap
params.description: If set to 1, the parent map is inherited by helper. Defaults to 0.

params.name: Immortal
params.description: If set to 1, the helper's life can't be reduced to 0. Defaults to 0.

params.name: InheritChannels
params.description: If set to 1, helper shares parent's sound channels. Setting it to 2 does the same thing but for root instead of parent. Defaults to 0.

params.name: InheritJuggle
params.description: If set to 1, helper's attacks also update parent's target list and add to the parent's juggle points. Also, the helper will inherit its parent's juggle points against attacked enemy. Setting it to 2 does the same thing but for root instead of parent. Defaults to 0.

params.name: KOVelocity
params.description: If set to 1, the helper will be affected by increased KO Velocity (defeated character flying across the screen), just like normal player. Defaults to 0.

params.name: Map
params.description: A helper's maps can be set immediately upon its creation via `map.<mapname>` syntax.

params.name: OwnClsnScale
params.description: A helper with this parameter will have its collision box scale be based on its own `size.xscale` and `size.yscale` constants rather than its root's.

params.name: OwnProjectile
params.description: A helper with this parameter can own its own projectiles instead of the root player. Note: If a helper is destroyed while a projectile is still active, the orphaned projectile loses its ability to interact with other players.

params.name: Preserve
params.description: If set to 1, the helper won't be destroyed after skipping round 1 intro and will move over to the next round, just like normal player. Defaults to 0.

params.name: Size
params.description: New size constants like `depth` and `weight` can also be attributed to helpers upon their creation, with the `size` prefix.

params.name: Standby
params.description: Helpers inherit standby flag from root characters. By using this parameter, a character can force a specific standby for its helper, regardless of the standby value of the character itself.

sctrls.example:
type = Helper
size.weight = 200
size.depth = 10, 10

sctrls.name: HitAdd
sctrls.description: Adds to the current combo counter.

params.name: value
params.description: *add_count* specifies the number of hits to add to the current combo counter.

sctrls.name: HitBy
sctrls.description: Temporarily specifies the types of hits that are be allowed hit to the player.
changeNotes:
In Mugen, the behavior of `HitBy` (and `NotHitBy`) is not as documented. The player's invincibility is compared to the enemy's actual statetype instead of their Hitdef's `SCA` flags. If a character has `ikemenversion`, it will work as documented.

`HitBy` (and `NotHitBy`) now also accepts a syntax similar to `HitOverride`, using `attr` and `slot` instead of `value`. Every player has access to 8 individual slots (numbered 0 to 7). This new syntax is required to use the new features.

params.name: value
params.description: Only one of the above parameters can be specified. *attr_string* should be a standard hit attribute string.  See Details.

params.name: time
params.description: Specifies the number of game ticks that these HitBy attributes should be effective for. Defaults to 1.

params.name: clsn.group
params.description: Determines the type of Clsn box that is affected. Valid values are `All`, `None`, `Clsn1`, `Clsn2`, `Size` and `Dummy`. Defaults to `All`.

params.name: clsn.index
params.description: Determines the index of the Clsn box that is affected. Defaults to `-1` (all boxes).

params.name: Stack
params.description:
Using this parameter makes a vulnerability slot stack with other slots. This allows setting vulnerability combinations not previously possible in Mugen.

Example, make a player vulnerable to Standing Attacks and Air Projectiles:

params.name: PlayerNo
params.description: Using this parameter limits vulnerability to a specific player number.

params.name: PlayerID
params.description: Using this parameter limits vulnerability to a specific player ID.

sctrls.example:
; Can be hit only by standing normal attacks  
trigger1 = 1  
type = HitBy  
value = S, NA

sctrls.name: HitDef
sctrls.description: Defines a single hit of the player's attack. If the player's Clsn1 box (red) comes in contact with his opponent's Clsn2 box (blue), and the HitDef was define on or before that particular point in time, then the specified effect will be applied. This is one of the more complex, but most commonly-used controllers. A single HitDef is valid only for a single hit. To make a move hit several times, you must trigger more than one HitDef during the attack.
changeNotes:
See `ground.cornerpush.velmul`.

See `ground.cornerpush.velmul`.

In Mugen, the `air.juggle` parameter is only used by the `Projectile` state controller. Characters with `ikemenversion` can now use this parameter in a `Hitdef` to update their juggle points. This allows a move with multiple hits to have different juggle properties in every hit, for instance.

This parameter now takes a third value, It specifies the z velocity.

See `ground.cornerpush.velmul`.

Determines friction to apply to cornerpush. Setting to `-1` makes friction depend on the target's statetype. Defaults to -1 for Ikemen characters and 0.7 for Mugen characters.

See `ground.cornerpush.velmul`.
