sctrls.name: ModifyText
sctrls.description: Using this state controller will update the specified parameters for the texts with the specified ID. Syntax is essentially the same as for Text sctrl.

params.name: ID
params.description: The ID of the texts to modify. Defaults to -1 (all the player's texts)

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the texts to modify. Defaults to -1 (all the player's texts)

params.name: removetime
params.description: The text will be removed after having been displayed for *rem_time* number of game ticks. Defaults to 1.

params.name: layerno
params.description: Sets the layer to which the text will be drawn on. 0 is in front of the background, but behind the players. 1 is in front of the players, but behind the foreground. 2 is in front of the foreground. Defaults to 1.

params.name: localcoord
params.description: Sets custom localcoord. If omitted, lifebar font defaults to the lifebar localcoord, character font and debug font defaults to the screen localcoord.

params.name: text
params.description: Text to be rendered. Defaults to "%v" (rendering first *params* argument of any type). *format_string* must be encased in double-quotes. It is a *printf* format string. You can use \t to generate a tab character (tab width is equivalent to 4 characters) and \n to break lines. To display the value of an arithmetic expression, you can put a %d (for ints) or a %f (for floats) in the format string, then specify the expression in the params list. To display a % character, you must put %% in the format string. Accepted format specifiers: %v (any type), %d, %i, %f, %F, %e, %E, %g, or %G. Syntax such as %0.2f is also supported.

params.name: params
params.description: Unlimited amount of numeric arguments can be specified in the format string. These should be listed under the params item, in order. The type of each parameter must match its format specifier.

params.name: font
params.description: *font_no* specifies the number of the font to use for text rendering. The 'F' prefix is optional: if included, then the text is rendred using lifebar (fight.def) fonts. Otherwise font [declared](https://github.com/ikemen-engine/Ikemen-GO/wiki/Character-features#def_files_font) in character's DEF file is used. If specified font doesn't exist than the debug font is used. Defaults to debug font.

params.name: bank
params.description: Color bank of the font to use. Refer to the font for what color banks it has. Defaults to 0.

params.name: align
params.description: *alignment* is a number representing the text alignment. 1 is left, 0 means center, and -1 is for right-alignment. Defaults to 1.

params.name: angle
params.description: Specify the rotation, rotation point is based on the text's alignment. Defaults to 0.

params.name: pos
params.description: Specify the offset at which to create the text. Defaults to 0,0.

params.name: scale
params.description: Specify the scaling factors to apply to the text in the horizontal and vertical directions. Defaults to 1,1.

params.name: color
params.description: Color adjustment values for the font. Defaults to 256,256,256,256 (no color adjustment).

params.name: textspacing
params.description: Specifies extra spacing between letters (*x_spacing*) and extra spacing between lines when `\n` is used to break lines (*y_spacing*). These values are added on top of the font’s DEF Spacing values.

params.name: textdelay
params.description: Adjusts the text typing time, the longer the time the longer the delay between each letter typed.

params.name: velocity
params.description: Applies speed to text on the defined axis.

params.name: accel
params.description: Applies acceleration to text on the defined axis.

params.name: friction
params.description: Applies friction to text on the defined axis (Friction value example: 0.95).

params.name: xshear
params.description: Specifies the amount of horizontal shearing to apply to the text. Defaults to 0.

params.name: maxdist
params.description:
Specifies the maximum velocity beyond which additional velocity will no longer be applied. Defaults to 0 (unlimited).

**palfx.key** The text sctrl can accept all the same key values from [PalFX state controller](http://www.elecbyte.com/mugendocs/sctrls.html#palfx)

params.name: hidewithbars
params.description: Enabling this parameter hides the text automatically when the fight screen is hidden.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = ModifyText
trigger = 1
ID = 50   ;Modify text with this ID
index = 0 ;Modify the first instance of this text
velocity = .3, 0
scale = 4, 4
params = animElemNo(0) ;Update params

sctrls.name: MoveHitReset
sctrls.description: Resets the movehit flag to 0. That is, after executing MoveHitReset, the triggers MoveContact, MoveGuarded, and MoveHit will all return 0.

sctrls.name: NotHitBy
sctrls.description: Temporarily specifies types of hits that are not allowed to hit the player.

params.name: value
params.description: Only one of the above parameters can be specified. *attr_string* should be a standard hit attribute string. See details.

params.name: time
params.description: Specifies the number of game ticks that these NotHitBy attributes should be effective for. Defaults to 1.

sctrls.example:
; Not hit by anything  
trigger1 = 1  
type = NotHitBy  
value = SCA  
  
; Not hit by normal attacks, and all projectiles  
trigger1 = 1  
type = NotHitBy  
value = , NA, AP

sctrls.name: Null
sctrls.description: Does nothing. May be used for disabling other state controllers by changing their type to Null.

sctrls.name: Offset
sctrls.description: Changes the player's display offset. The player is drawn shifted from his axis by this amount.

params.name: y
params.description: Specifies the x and y offsets, respectively. You can specify one or both of the optional parameters.

sctrls.name: OverrideClsn
sctrls.description: This state controller allows you to directly modify a player’s collision boxes without changing their animation.

params.name: group
params.description: The type of collision box to override. Valid values: `All` (nightly build only), `None`, `Clsn1`, `Clsn2`, `Size` and `Dummy` (nightly build only). Using `None` removes all active Clsn overrides. Defaults to `None`.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the box to modify. Use `-1` to affect all boxes. Using an out-of-bounds index will append a new box. Defaults to `0`.

params.name: rect
params.description: The rectangle, or coordinates for the box. Using `0, 0, 0, 0` removes the box.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]; Force player to have at least one Clsn1 box
type = OverrideClsn
trigger1 = 1
group = Clsn1
index = 0
rect = 0, -100, 50, -50

sctrls.name: PalFX
sctrls.description: Applies temporary effects the player's palette. These will also affect the palette of any explods and helpers the player owns, unless they have set `ownpal` to a nonzero value.

params.name: time
params.description: Specifies the number of ticks that the palette effects should last. Specify -1 to have the palette effects last indefinitely. Specify 0 to stop any ongoing palette effects.

params.name: mul
params.description: Each add component is added to the appropriate component of the player's palette, and the result is multiplied by the appropriate mul component divided by 256. For instance, if *pal_r* is the red component of the character's original palette, then the new red component is (*pal_r* + *add_r*) \* *mul_r* / 256. The values for mul must be >= 0. The defaults for these parameters are for no change, i.e. add = 0, 0, 0 and mul = 256,256,256.

params.name: sinadd
params.description: Creates an additional sine-wave palette addition effect. Period specifies the period of the sine wave in game ticks, and the amplitude parameters control the amplitude of the sine wave for the respective components. For instance, if t represents the number of ticks elapsed since the activation of the PalFX controller, and *pal_r* is the red component of the character's original palette, then the red component of the character's palette at time t is (*pal_r* + *add_r* + *ampl_r* \* sin(2 \* pi \* t / *period*)) \* *mul_r* / 256.

params.name: invertall
params.description: If *bvalue* is non-zero, then the colors in the palette will be inverted, creating a `film negative` effect. Color inversion is applied before effects of add and mul. *bvalue* defaults to 0.

params.name: color
params.description: This affects the color level of the palette. If value is 0, the palette will be greyscale. If *value* is 256, there is no change in palette. Values in between will have an intermediate effect. This parameter's effects are applied before invertall, add and mul. Values must be in range 0 to 256. Default value is 256.

params.name: invertblend
params.description:
Inverts current blend mode if enabled so Sub becomes Add and Add becomes Sub.

For PalFx it accepts 4 values:
* 0 = Disabled (Mugen 1.0 blending behavior)
* 1 = Enabled (Mugen 1.0 blending behavior)
* -1 = Disabled (Mugen 1.1 blending behavior)
* 2 = Enabled (Mugen 1.1 blending behavior)

If character MugenVersion is 1.1 and invertall = 1 and if invertblend param is omitted, it inverts blend by default. For all other MugenVersion invertblend is 0 if omitted.

params.name: hue
params.description: This affects the hue level of the palette. Avaiable range is -256 to 256.

params.name: sinmul
params.description: Similliar to "sinadd" parameter but instead it creates effect related to "mul" parameter.

params.name: sincolor
params.description: Similliar to "sinadd" parameter but instead it creates effect related to "color" parameter.

params.name: sinhue
params.description: Similliar to "sinadd" parameter but instead it creates effect related to "hue" parameter.

sctrls.name: ParentMapAdd
sctrls.description: If the player is a helper, adds value to parent's map. If the player is not a helper, this controller does nothing. Parent refers to the instance that spawned the helper.

params.name: map
params.description: Specifies a name of the map that we add value to.

params.name: value
params.description: *expr* is the value to add to the map.

sctrls.name: ParentMapSet
sctrls.description: If the player is a helper, sets value to parent's map. If the player is not a helper, this controller does nothing. Parent refers to the instance that spawned the helper.

params.name: map
params.description: Specifies a name of the map that we assign value to.

params.name: value
params.type: int or float, or string in nightly build
params.description: *expr* is the value to assign to the map.

sctrls.name: ParentVarAdd
sctrls.description: If the player is a helper, adds to one of the player's parent's working variables. Either a float variable or an int variable can be added to by this controller. If the player is not a helper, this controller does nothing.

params.name: v
params.description: *var_no* should evaluate to an integer between 0 and 59.

params.name: value
params.description:
*int_expr* is the value to add to the int variable indicated by *var_no*.

*float_expr* is the value to add to the float variable indexed by *var_no*.

params.name: fv
params.description: *var_no* should evaluate to an integer between 0 and 39.

sctrls.name: ParentVarSet
sctrls.description: If the player is a helper, sets one of the parent's working variables. Either a float variable or an int variable can be set by this controller. Does nothing if the player is not a helper.

params.name: v
params.description: *var_no* should evaluate to an integer between 0 and 59.

params.name: value
params.description:
*int_expr* is the value to assign to the int variable indicated by *var_no*.

*float_expr* is the value to assign to the float variable indexed by *var_no*.

params.name: fv
params.description: *var_no* should evaluate to an integer between 0 and 39.

sctrls.name: Pause
sctrls.description: Pauses the game for the specified amount of time. Player and background updates are not carried out during this time.

params.name: time
params.description: This is the number of game ticks to pause for. Valid values for *t* are all positive numbers, starting from 0.

params.name: endcmdbuftime
params.description: This is the number of ticks during the end of the pause in which the player's move commands will be buffered. Buffered commands will be detected by the `command` trigger immediately after the pause ends. The buffering applies only to players who are unable to move during the pause (see movetime parameter). Valid values for endcmdbuftime are from 0 to *t*, where *t* is the value of the time parameter. Defaults to 0.

params.name: movetime
params.description: This is the number of ticks during the start of the pause in which the player is allowed to move. Collision detection is carried out during this time, so it is possible to hit other players. Valid values for *mt* are from 0 to *t*, where *t* is the value of the time parameter. Defaults to 0.

params.name: pausebg
params.description: If set to 1, the background is stopped during the pause. If 0, the background continues updating during the pause. Defaults to 1.

sctrls.name: PlayBgm
sctrls.description:
Plays back music. Supported file formats: *mp3*, *ogg*, *wav*, *flac*, *mid*, *midi*, *xm*, *mod*, *it*, *s3m*.

Music can be specified directly with the *bgm* parameter or loaded from existing game music definitions with the *source* parameter.

params.name: source
params.description:
Loads the BGM and its associated parameters from an existing music definition. Valid music sources are:
* `match`: music assigned to the current match. This is the final music list after stage, character, stage selection and launch parameters have been merged according to their priorities. This is normally the appropriate source when restoring the match's stage music after temporarily playing another BGM.
* `stagedef`: music declared in the current stage DEF file.
* `charparams`: music assigned through the character's select.def parameters.
* `stageparams`: music assigned through the stage's select.def parameters.
* `launchparams`: music assigned through launch parameters.
* `motif`: music…

params.name: bgm
params.description: Path of the music file to play. Leave it blank if you want to stop current music. *bgm_path* file lookup checks paths relative to the character's directory, current stage directory, top Ikemen directory and *data* directory, with *sound* directory lookup also supported.

params.name: loop
params.description: Set *loop_flag* to a nonzero value to have the BGM loop over and over, or 0 to disable looping. Defaults to 1.

params.name: volume
params.description: Adjust the volume. 100 is for 100%. Defaults to 100. If no new BGM is successfully selected, *volume_scale* alters volume for currently playing BGM.

params.name: loopstart
params.description: Loop start position sample number.

params.name: loopend
params.description: Loop end position sample number.

params.name: startposition
params.description: Sample point where the music should start playing.

params.name: freqmul
params.description: Frequency multiplier of the BGM (controls pitch & tempo). Defaults to 1.0.

params.name: loopcount
params.description: Changes the number of times this BGM should loop. A negative value makes it loop indefinitely. Defaults to -1.

sctrls.name: PlayerPush
sctrls.description: Disables the player's push checking for one tick. Push checking keeps players from overlapping one another. By temporarily disabling push checking, dodge-type moves in which the player passes through another (but can still be hit) can be implemented.

params.name: value
params.description: If *push_flag* is nonzero, then push checking is enabled. If *push_flag* is zero, then push checking is disabled.

params.name: Priority
params.description: `PlayerPush` now accepts a `priority` parameter. A player with a higher priority can't be pushed by a player with a lower priority and will also push them out of a stage corner. Priority is reset to 0 every frame.

params.name: AffectTeam
params.description:
specifies which team's players can be push.

- F : Allows only allies to be pushed out (enemies will pass through)
- B : Pushes both allies and enemies
- E : Pushes only enemies (default)

sctrls.name: PlaySnd
sctrls.description: Plays back a sound.

params.name: value
params.description: *group_no* and *sound_no* correspond to the identifying pair that you assigned each sound in the player's snd file. To play back a sound from `common.snd`, precede group_no with an `F`.

params.name: volumescale
params.description: *volume_scale* controls the volume of the sound. A value of 100 specifies 100% volume, 50 for 50%, and so on. Valid values are from 0 to 100. Defaults to 100.

params.name: channel
params.description: *channel_no* specifies which of the player's sound channels the sound should play on. Only one voice may play on a particular channel at a time. For example, if you play a sound on channel 2, then play any sound on the same channel before the first sound is done, then by default the first sound is stopped as the second one plays. 0 is a special channel reserved for player voices. Channel 0 voices are stopped when the player is hit. It's recommended you play your character's voice sounds on channel 0. If omitted, *channel_no* defaults to -1, meaning the sound will play on any free channel.

params.name: lowpriority
params.description: This is only valid if the channel is not -1. If *pr* is nonzero, then a sound currently playing on this sound's channel (from a previous PlaySnd call) cannot be interrupted by this sound.

params.name: freqmul
params.description: The sound frequency will be multiplied by *f*. For example. Setting *f* to 1.1 will result in a higher-pitched sound. Defaults to 1.0 (no change in frequency).

params.name: loop
params.description: Set *loop_flag* to a nonzero value to have the sound sample loop over and over. Defaults to 0.

params.name: pan
params.description: This is the positional offset of the sound, measured in pixels. If *p* > 0, then the sound is offset to the front of the player. If *p* < 0, then sound is offset to the back. Defaults to 0. This parameter is mutually exclusive with abspan.

params.name: abspan
params.description: Like pan, except the sound is panned from the center of the screen, not from the player's position. This parameter is mutually exclusive with pan.

params.name: Priority
params.description: Sets the priority of the sound. Does nothing when channel is not specified. A sound with higher priority will not be interrupted by sounds with lower priority. Defaults to 0.

params.name: LoopStart
params.description: Sets the sample to begin looping from.

params.name: LoopEnd
params.description: Sets the sample to end looping at.

params.name: StartPosition
params.description: Sets the sample to begin playing from.

params.name: LoopCount
params.description: If set, will play the sound *loop_count* number of times before stopping. Nonzero values take precedence over the `loop` parameter.

params.name: StopOnGetHit
params.description: This parameter makes the sound be interrupted if the player gets hit. Defaults to 1 if channel is set to 0.

params.name: StopOnChangeState
params.description: This parameter makes the sound be interrupted if the player changes states.

sctrls.example:
; Plays back sound 2,0 from the player's SND file  
type = PlaySnd  
value = 2,0  
  
; Plays back sound 5,2 from fight.snd  
type = PlaySnd  
value = F5,2

sctrls.name: PosAdd
sctrls.description: Offsets the player's position by the specified amounts. The X coordinate is relative to the player's axis, with positive values moving in the direction that the player is facing. The Y coordinate is relative to the player's axis, with negative values moving up.

params.name: x
params.description: Moves the player *x_value* pixels forward. Defaults to 0.

params.name: y
params.description: Moves the player *y_value* pixels downwards. Defaults to 0.

sctrls.name: PosFreeze
sctrls.description: Temporarily freezes the player's position.

params.name: value
params.description: If *freeze_flag* is non-zero, the player's position will be frozen, else it will not be. Defaults to 1.

sctrls.name: PosSet
sctrls.description: Sets the player's position to the specified coordinates. The X coordinate is relative to the center of the screen, with positive values moving right. The Y coordinate is relative to the floor, with negative values moving up.

params.name: x
params.description: Specifies the new x-position of the player.

params.name: y
params.description: Specifies the new y-position of the player.

sctrls.name: PowerAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the specified amount to the player's power.

params.name: value
params.description: *add_amt* is the number to add to the player's power.

sctrls.name: PowerSet
sctrls.description: Sets the amount of power that the player has.

params.name: value
params.description: *pow_amt* is the new value to set the player's power to.

sctrls.name: PrintToConsole
sctrls.description:
This controller is only useful for debugging. PrintToConsole prints a specified message to debug mode console, as well as terminal / command line window, if it's opened.

The syntax is the same as DisplayToClipboard:

params.name: text
params.description:
*format_string* must be encased in double-quotes. It is a printf format string, so if you know about printf, you can skip this description. The format string contains any text you wish to display. You can also use \n to generate a line break, and \t to generate a tab character (tab width is equivalent to 4 characters). To display the value of an arithmetic expression, you can put a %d (for ints) or a %f (for floats) in the format string, then specify the expression in the params list. To display a % character, you must put %% in the format string.

Following format specifiers are accepted: %v (any type), %d, %i, %f, %F, %e, %E, %g, or %G. Format specifier syntax such as %0.2f is also…

params.name: params
params.description:
Unlimited amount of numeric arguments can be specified in the format string. These should be listed under the params item, in order. The type of each parameter must match its format specifier. You cannot specify more or less parameters than are called for in the format string.

If there is a type mismatch between the format specifier and the parameter actually provided, then the actual value of the parameter will be shown in an appropriate form for that type, using default formatting options.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = PrintToConsole
text = "The value of var(17) is %d, which is %f%% of 23.\n\t--Kiwi."
params = var(17):=1,var(17)/.230

; prints the following to console:
;The value of var(17) is 1, which is 4.347826% of 23.
;	--Kiwi.

sctrls.name: Projectile
sctrls.description: Creates a projectile for the player. The Projectile controller takes all the parameters of the HitDef controller, which control the HitDef for the projectile. In addition, Projectile has the following additional parameters:
changeNotes: In MUGEN, contrary to its documentation, projectiles do not support the ChainID and NochainID parameters. This behavior has been replicated by default in Ikemen GO. However, when a character's `ikemenversion` is not 0, projectiles do take these parameters into account.

params.name: ProjID
params.description: Specifies an ID number to refer to this projectile by. Should be positive, if specified.

params.name: projanim
params.description: Specifies the animation action number to use for the projectile's animation. Defaults to 0 if omitted.

params.name: projhitanim
params.description: Specifies the animation action number to play when the projectile hits the opponent. Defaults to -1 (no change in animation) if omitted.

params.name: projremanim
params.description: Specifies the animation action number to play when the projectile is removed (due to its time expiring or hitting the its removal boundaries, etc). If omitted, projhitanim is used instead.

params.name: projcancelanim
params.description: Specifies the animation action number to play when the projectile is cancelled by hitting another projectile. If omitted, projremanim is used instead.

params.name: projscale
params.description: Specifies the scale factor of the projectile. The final scale of the projectile is affected by both this parameter and the `proj.doscale` parameter in the [Size] group of p1's constants file. Defaults to `1, 1` (normal size) if omitted.

params.name: projremove
params.description: Set to a non-zero value to have the projectile be removed after it hits, or to 0 to disable this behavior. Defaults to 1.

params.name: projremovetime
params.description: Specifies the number of ticks after which the projectile should be removed from the screen. If -1, the projectile will not be removed. Defaults to -1.

params.name: velocity
params.description: Specifies the initial x and y velocities for the projectile to travel at. Defaults to `0, 0` if omitted.

params.name: remvelocity
params.description: Specifies the x and y velocities at which the projectile should travel while being removed. Defaults to `0, 0` if omitted.

params.name: accel
params.description: Specifies the acceleration to apply to the projectile in the x and y directions. Defaults to `0, 0` if omitted.

params.name: velmul
params.description: Specifies x and y velocity multipliers. The projectile's velocity is multiplied by these multipliers on every tick. The multipliers default to 1 if omitted.

params.name: projhits
params.description: Specifies the number of hits that the projectile can impart on an opponent before it is removed. Defaults to 1.

params.name: projmisstime
params.description: If the projectile is configured for multiple hits, *miss_time* specifies the number of ticks after each hit before the projectile can hit again. Defaults to 0.

params.name: projpriority
params.description: Specifies the projectile priority. If the projectile collides with another projectile of equal priority, they will cancel. If it collides with another of lower priority, it will cancel the lower-priority projectile, and the higher-priority one will have its priority decreased by 1. Defaults to 1.

params.name: projsprpriority
params.description: Specifies the sprite priority of the projectile. Higher-priority sprites are drawn on top of lower-priority sprites. Defaults to 3.

params.name: projedgebound
params.description: Specifies the distance off the edge of the screen before the projectile is automatically removed. Units are in pixels. Defaults to 40 in 240p, 80 in 480p, 160 in 720p.

params.name: projstagebound
params.description: Specifies the greatest distance the projectile can travel off the edge of the stage before being it is automatically removed. Defaults to 40 in 240p, 80 in 480p, 160 in 720p.

params.name: projheightbound
params.description: Specifies the least and greatest y values the projectile is allowed to reach. If the projectile leaves these boundaries, it is automatically removed. Note: since y values decrease with increasing height on the screen, lowbound actually specifies the greatest height the projectile can attain. *lowbound* defaults to -240 in 240p, -480 in 480p, -960 in 720p. *highbound* defaults to 1 in 240p, 2 in 480p, 4 in 720p.

params.name: offset
params.description: Specifies the x and y offsets at which the projectile should be created. Both parameters default to 0 if omitted. Projectiles are always created facing the same direction as the player. *off_x* is in relation to the direction the projectile is facing. The exact behavior of the offset parameters is dependent on the postype.

params.name: postype
params.description:
*postype_string* specifies the postype -- how to interpret the pos parameters. In all cases, a positive y offset means a downward displacement. In all cases, *off_y* is relative to the position of the player.

Valid values for *postype_string* are the following:

**p1**

Interprets offset relative to p1's axis. A positive *off_x* is toward the front of p1. This is the default value for postype.

**p2**

Interprets offset relative to p2's axis. A positive *off_x* is toward the front of p1.  If p2 does not exist, the position is calculated with respect to p1 and a warning is logged.

**front**

Interprets *off_x* relative to the edge of the screen that p1 is facing toward. A positive *off_x*…

params.name: projshadow
params.description: If *shadow* is not 0, a shadow will be drawn for the explod, else no shadow will be drawn. Defaults to 0.

params.name: supermovetime
params.description: Specifies the number of ticks that the projectile will be unfrozen during a SuperPause. Defaults to 0.

params.name: pausemovetime
params.description: Specifies the number of ticks that the projectile will be unfrozen during a Pause. Defaults to 0.

params.name: ownpal
params.description:
If *ownpal_flag* is 0, the projectile will be affected by subsequent execution of its owner's PalFX and RemapPal controllers. This is the default.

If *ownpal_flag* is 1, the projectile will not be affected by its owner's PalFX and RemapPal controllers.

params.name: remappal
params.description: Forces a palette remap of the projectile's indexed-color sprites to the specified palette. This parameter is used only if *ownpal_flag* is non-zero. If *dst_pal_grp* is -1, this parameter will be ignored. Defaults to `-1, 0`.

params.name: afterimage.time
params.description:
See below.

**afterimage.length**

See below.

**afterimage....**

If included, these parameters add afterimage effects to the projectile. The parameters are the same as in the AfterImage controller, except these are all prepended with `afterimage.`

params.name: ProjAngle
params.description: Specifies the angle to rotate the Projectile animation.

params.name: ProjXAngle
params.description: Specifies the Xangle of the Projectile animation.

params.name: ProjYAngle
params.description: Specifies the Yangle of the Projectile animation.

params.name: ProjClsnAngle
params.description: Defines the angle for the projectile's collision boxes. In degrees.

params.name: ProjClsnScale
params.description: Defines the collision box scale for the projectile.

params.name: ProjDepthBound
params.description: Like `projedgebound` but for the Z space. Determines how far out of the Z boundaries the projectile can travel before being removed.

params.name: ProjLayerNo
params.description: Specify on which layer the projectile should be drawn. Valid values are -1, 0 and 1. Defaults to the same layer as the player.

params.name: ProjFocalLength
params.description: Focal Length of the projection. Does nothing when projection is not perspective or perspective2.

params.name: ProjProjection
params.description:
Affect how the projectile is drawn when xangle or yangle is not zero.

- orthographic: The default value, the projectile is drawn using orthographic projection.
- perspective: The projectile is drawn using perspective projection. Distortion is affected by the position of the sprite relative to the center of the screen.
- perspective2: The projectile is drawn using perspective projection. Distortion is affected by the position of the sprite relative to the center of the animation.

params.name: ProjReflection
params.description: If 0, disables reflection on the projectile regardless of its shadow color. If 1, enables reflection on the projectile regardless of its shadow color. Defaults to showing a reflection if the projectile's shadow is not 0, 0, 0.

params.name: ProjWindow
params.description: This parameter takes four numbers (similar to the format of a Clsn box) which forms a rectangle outside of which the pixels will not be rendered.

params.name: ProjXshear
params.description: Specifies the amount of horizontal shearing to apply to the projectile. Defaults to 0.

params.name: Shader
params.description:
Specifying the name of the currently loaded custom shader will apply that shader to Projectile.

Note: In the nightly build the syntax changed to `shader.name`.

params.name: ShaderTime
params.description:
Specifying this parameter will remove the custom shader after it has been displayed for the specified number of ticks. The default value is -1.

Note: In the nightly build the syntax changed to `shader.time`.

params.name: ShaderParam.pX
params.description:
Specifies the value to send to the custom shader. The value specified here can be used as a variable within the custom shader. X is limited to 0 to 15, and a maximum of 16 values ​​can be sent.

Note: In the nightly build the syntax changed to `shader.paramX`.

params.name: ShaderTexX.spr
params.description: Note: In the nightly build the syntax changed to `shader.texX.spr`.

params.name: ShaderTexX.anim
params.description:
Specifies the texture to send to the custom shader. The sprites specified here can be used as textures within the custom shader. You can specify 1 or 2 for X, and send up to two sprites. Each tex can be assigned either a sprite number (spr) or an anim number. It is not possible to assign both sprite and anim numbers to the same tex number simultaneously. Note that since textures are loaded as raw data, images with palettes may not display correctly as is.

Note: In the nightly build the syntax changed to `shader.texX.anim`.

params.name: shader.playerno
params.description: Specifies the player number who owns the shader to be used. Defaults to own player number.

params.name: shader.shadow
params.description: Specifies if the projectile shadow is affected by the shader. Defaults to 1.

params.name: shader.reflection
params.description: Specifies if the projectile reflection is affected by the shader. Defaults to 1.

params.name: shader.afterimage
params.description: Specifies if the projectile afterimage is affected by the shader. Defaults to 1.

sctrls.name: RedLifeAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the specified amount to the player's red life, scaled by the player's defense multiplier if necessary.

params.name: value
params.description: *add_amt* is the number to add to the player's red life.

params.name: absolute
params.description: If *abs_flag* is 1, then *add_amt* will not be scaled (i.e. attack and defense multipliers will be ignored). Defaults to 0.

sctrls.example: redLifeAdd{value: 10; absolute: 1}

sctrls.name: RedLifeSet
sctrls.description: Sets the amount of red life that the player has.

params.name: value
params.description: *set_amt* is the new value to set the player's red life to.

sctrls.example: redLifeSet{value: 100}

sctrls.name: RemapPal
sctrls.description: Changes one of the player's palettes to another.

params.name: dest
params.description:
All of the player sprites that use the source palette will be drawn using the dest palette instead. The source and dest palettes must exist within the player's sprites, and both must be of the same color depth.

If *src_pal_grp* is -1, all indexed-color sprites will be remapped to the dest palette. This only affects sprites of the same color depth as the dest palette. All other existing mappings will be removed.

If *dst_pal_grp* is -1, the mapping for the source is removed. Setting the dest pair to the same values as the source pair has the same effect.

The default value for source is -1,0. The default value for dest is -1,0.

sctrls.example:
; All sprites using palette (1,1) will be drawn using palette (1,3)  
; instead.  
type = RemapPal  
source = 1,1  
dest = 1,3

sctrls.name: RemapSprite
sctrls.description: Remaps one sprite with another (or does this for multiple sprites at once, based on character's CNS [RemapPreset](https://github.com/ikemen-engine/Ikemen-GO/wiki/Character-features#cns_remappreset) data)

params.name: reset
params.description: Set to 1 to reset all existing sprite remaps. Defaults to 0.

params.name: preset
params.description: Name of the character's CNS `RemapPreset` data.

params.name: dest
params.description: Any animation that references source sprite will be drawn using the dest sprite instead. Note that the dest sprite group number and item refers to an unmapped sprite numbers.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = RemapSprite
trigger1 = var(10)=1
preset = "MyTransformation"
reset = 1

sctrls.name: RemoveExplod
sctrls.description: Removes all of a player's explods, or just the explods with a specified ID number.

params.name: ID
params.description: *remove_id* is the ID number of the explods to remove. If omitted, removes all explods owned by the player.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the explod to be affected. Defaults to -1 (all).

sctrls.name: RemoveStoryboard
sctrls.description: Removes all of a player's storyboards, or just the storyboards with a specified ID number.

params.name: ID
params.description: remove_id is the ID number of the storyboard to remove. If omitted, removes all storyboards owned by the player.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = RemoveStoryboard
trigger1 = time = 30
ID = 10

sctrls.name: RemoveText
sctrls.description: Removes all of a player's texts, or just the texts with a specified ID number.

params.name: ID
params.description: remove_id is the ID number of the texts to remove. If omitted, removes all texts owned by the player.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = RemoveText
trigger1 = time = 30
ID = 10

sctrls.name: ReversalDef
sctrls.description:
Defines a reversal. If one of P2's Clns1 boxes comes in contact with one of P1's Clsn1 boxes and a ReversalDef is active, then P1 will reverse P2's attack. Use with p1stateno (and optionally p2stateno) for creating reversal attacks.

ReversalDefs take the HitDef parameters pausetime, sparkno, hitsound, p1stateno, and p2stateno, plus:
changeNotes: ReversalDef can also use the new HitDef parameters. In addition it has the following exclusive parameters.

params.name: reversal.attr
params.description: *attr_string* specifies the list of attack attributes that can be reversed by this ReversalDef. It is a standard hit attribute string. For instance, `reversal.attr = SA,NA,SA` means stand+air, normal attack, special attack.

params.name: reversal.guardflag
params.description: Only hits containing the specified flags in their `guardflag` will be countered.

params.name: reversal.guardflag.not
params.description: Hits containing the specified flags in their `guardflag` will not be countered.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]; Counter attacks that can be blocked crouching but not standing (lows)
type = ReversalDef
trigger1 = 1
reversal.attr = SCA, AA
reversal.guardflag = L
reversal.guardflag.not = H

sctrls.name: RootMapAdd
sctrls.description: If the player is a helper, adds value to root's map. If the player is not a helper, this controller does nothing. Root refers to the main player.

params.name: map
params.description: Specifies a name of the map that we add value to.

params.name: value
params.description: *expr* is the value to add to the map.

sctrls.example: rootMapAdd{map: "example"; value: 1}

sctrls.name: RootMapSet
sctrls.description: If the player is a helper, sets value root's map. If the player is not a helper, this controller does nothing. Root refers to the main player.

params.name: map
params.description: Specifies a name of the map that we assign value to.

params.name: value
params.type: int or float, or string in nightly build
params.description: *expr* is the value to assign to the map.

sctrls.example: rootMapSet{map: "example"; value: 1}

sctrls.name: RootVarAdd
sctrls.description:
If the player is a helper, adds value to root's working variables. Either a float variable or an int variable can be added by this controller. If the player is not a helper, this controller does nothing. Root refers to the main player.

Required parameters (int version):

params.name: v
params.description: *var_no* should evaluate to an integer between 0 and 59.

params.name: value
params.description:
*int_expr* is the value to add to the int variable indicated by var_no.

Required parameters (float version): *float_expr* is the value to add to the float variable indicated by var_no.

params.name: fv
params.description: *var_no* should evaluate to an integer between 0 and 39.

sctrls.example: rootVarAdd{v: 0; value: 1}

sctrls.name: RootVarSet
sctrls.description:
If the player is a helper, sets value root's working variables. Either a float variable or an int variable can be set by this controller. If the player is not a helper, this controller does nothing. Root refers to the main player.

Required parameters (int version):

params.name: v
params.description: *var_no* should evaluate to an integer between 0 and 59.

params.name: value
params.description:
*int_expr* is the value to assign to the int variable indicated by var_no.

Required parameters (float version): *float_expr* is the value to assign to the float variable indicated by var_no.

params.name: fv
params.description: *var_no* should evaluate to an integer between 0 and 39.

sctrls.example: rootVarSet{v: 0; value: 1}

sctrls.name: RoundTimeAdd
sctrls.description: Add specified amount of ticks into round time.

params.name: value
params.description: add_ticks specifies the number of ticks that should be added to round time.

sctrls.example: roundTimeAdd{value: 60}

sctrls.name: RoundTimeSet
sctrls.description: Set round time to specified amount of ticks.

params.name: value
params.description: set_ticks specifies the number of ticks that should be set as a current round time.

sctrls.example: roundTimeSet{value: 60}

sctrls.name: RunState
sctrls.description: Allows executing a state's code without changing the player's current state. Works with negative states.

params.name: value
params.description: The state number to run.

params.name: playerno
params.description: Whose player's states to use. Defaults to own player number.

sctrls.name: SaveFile
sctrls.description: Put specified data together and save it as binary. It uses gob, which is a serialized format for Go language, as the storage format. All characters specified by the character or helper who executed the function are stored at that time.

params.name: savedata
params.description: Specifies the data type that should be saved. Valid values for var_type are "var", "fvar", and "map".

params.name: path
params.description: Specifies the save destination file path (relative to the character folder). Can use any extension (.gob is recommended)

params.name: maps
params.description: A list of maps to load. Defaults to empty.

params.name: maps.include
params.description: All maps containing this string in their names will be saved. Defaults to empty.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = SaveFile
trigger1 = time = 10
savedata = var
path = "kfm.gob"

sctrls.name: ScoreAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the specified amount of points to P1 current score counter.

params.name: value
params.description: *expr* is the the number of score points to add to the P1 current score counter.

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = ScoreAdd
trigger1 = AnimElem = 21
value = 100

sctrls.name: ScreenBound
sctrls.description: Specifies whether or not the player's movement should be constrained to the screen or not. Also determines whether the camera should move to follow the player or not. The results of this controller are valid for 1 tick.

params.name: value
params.description: If *bound_flag* is 0, the player will be allowed to move off the screen. If 1, the player is constrained within the screen. Defaults to 0 if omitted.

params.name: movecamera
params.description: If 1, specifies that camera should pan to follow the player in the x direction and in the y direction, respectively. Defaults to 0 in both instances if omitted.

params.name: StageBound
params.description: Lets a character bypass leftbound and rightbound from stage.

sctrls.name: SelfState
sctrls.description: Like ChangeState, except that this changes a player back to a state in his own state data. Use this when you have placed an opponent player in a custom state via an attack, and wish to restore the opponent to his own states.

params.name: value
params.description: *state_no* is the number of the state to change to.

params.name: ReadPlayerID
params.description:
Change to the state of the character with the specified Player ID. If successful, it would take the character with the specified PlayerID to the selected state.

See also [ChangeState](sctrl#changed_changestate).

params.name: ctrl
params.description: *ctrl_flag* is the value to set the player's control flag to. 0 for no control, nonzero for control.

params.name: anim
params.description: This is the action number to switch to. If omitted, the player's animation will remain unchanged.

params.name: Continue
params.description: Due to the way State -1 is normally used to read inputs and change states, Mugen had it so that using a `ChangeState` in a negative state would stop the execution of the rest of the code in that state. Setting `Continue` to 1 will disable this behavior. When a `ChangeState` is redirected, `Continue` will default to 1.

sctrls.name: ShaderSet
sctrls.description: Sets the specified custom shader to the character.

params.name: shader
params.description:
Specify the name from the currently loaded custom shader.

Note: In the nightly build the syntax was changed to `name`.

params.name: time
params.description: The custom shader is displayed for the specified number of ticks before being removed. The default is 1. Specifying -1 will prevent it from being removed until ShaderSet is applied again.

params.name: shaderparam.pX
params.description:
Specifies the value to send to the custom shader. The value specified here can be used as a variable within the custom shader. X is limited to 0 to 15, and a maximum of 16 values ​​can be sent.

The shaderparam variable is defined within the custom shader, for example:

**OpenGL:**

params.name: shadertexX.anim
params.description:
Specifies the texture to send to the custom shader. The sprites specified here can be used as textures within the custom shader. You can specify 1 or 2 for X, and send up to two sprites. Each tex can be assigned either a sprite number (spr) or an anim number. It is not possible to assign both sprite and anim numbers to the same tex number simultaneously. Note that since textures are loaded as raw data, images with palettes may not display correctly as is.

Shadertex textures are defined within custom shaders, for example

Note: In the nightly build the syntax was changed to `texX.spr` and `texX.anim`.

**OpenGL:**

params.name: playerno
params.description: Specifies the player number who owns the shader to be used. Defaults to own player number.

params.name: shadow
params.description: Specifies if the shader also affects char shadow. Defaults to 1.

params.name: reflection
params.description: Specifies if the shader also affects char reflection. Defaults to 1.

params.name: afterimage
params.description: Specifies if the shader also affects char afterimage. Defaults to 1.

sctrls.name: ShiftInput
sctrls.description: Allows temporarily changing the function of the player's keys. Resets every frame.

params.name: input
params.description: The key to be changed

params.name: output
params.description:
The new function for that key

Valid keys are: U, D, L, R, a, b, c, x, y, z, s, d, w, m, none

Setting `input` and `output` both to `none` resets all buttons to normal state immediately.

sctrls.name: SndPan
sctrls.description: Changes the panning of a currently playing sound. This controller may be continually triggered to smoothly move a sound across the sound field or to have a sound follow the player.

params.name: channel
params.description: Specifies the channel number of the sound to pan.

params.name: pan
params.description: These parameters cannot both be specified at the same time. *p* determines the sound offset in pixels from the player (in the case of *pan*) or from the center of the screen (in the case of *abspan*). See PlaySnd for a description of the panning parameters.

sctrls.name: SprPriority
sctrls.description: Changes the player's sprite priority. Higher-priority sprites are drawn on top of lower-priority sprites.

params.name: value
params.description: Valid values are -5 to 5.

params.name: LayerNo
params.description: Change the layer number on which the player is drawn on. Valid values are -1, 0 and 1. Defaults to 0. [TODO - Link to explanation on layer drawing order]

sctrls.example:
[State Test]
type = SprPriority
trigger1 = Time = 0
value = 5
layerno = -1

sctrls.name: StateTypeSet
sctrls.description: Changes the current state type and move type. Useful for states that go from the ground into the air, etc.
changeNotes:
All parameters now accept string expressions.

Example: `statetype = ifelse(random < 500, "S", "C")`

params.changeNote: Type `U` can now also be used. Same functionality as in StateDef: keeps `stateType` unchanged. This change is mostly for the sake of source code consistency.
params.name: statetype
params.description: Set *state_type* to A for air, C for crouch, S for stand, or L for liedown. Defaults to no change.

params.changeNote: Type `U` can now also be used. Same functionality as in StateDef: keeps `moveType` unchanged. This change is mostly for the sake of source code consistency.
params.name: movetype
params.description: Set *move_type* to I for idle, A for attack, or H for gethit. Defaults to no change.

params.name: physics
params.description: Set *physics* to A for air, C for crouch, S for stand, or N for none. Defaults to no change.

sctrls.name: StopSnd
sctrls.description: Stops any sound which is playing on the specified channel.

params.changeNote: Mugen allowed stopping all sounds for all players with `channel = -1`, but had no way to stop only the player's own sound channels. Using `channel = -2` will now do just that.
params.name: channel
params.description: Stops playback of any sound on *chan_no*. If *chan_no* is -1, then all sounds are stopped, including those belonging to other players.

sctrls.name: Storyboard
sctrls.description: Plays the specified storyboard during a match. Each execution creates a separate instance, allowing several storyboards to play at once.

params.name: path
params.description: Specifies the path to the storyboard file. Relative paths are searched first from the character's directory, then from the Ikemen top-level directory.

params.name: id
params.description: Assigns an ID used by ModifyStoryboard and RemoveStoryboard. Defaults to 0. IDs are local to the character or helper that owns the instance; another player's storyboard with the same ID is unaffected.

params.name: space
params.description:
Specifies the coordinate space in which the storyboard is to be created. Valid values for `space` are:
* *none*
Uses the storyboard's normal rendering and coordinate system, without applying match placement or camera transforms. The `pos`, `scale`, `facing`, `bindID`, and `bindtime` parameters do not affect rendering in this space. This is the default.
* *screen*
This coordinate space maps to the screen. The upper-left corner is 0,0 and the lower-right corner is ScreenWidth,ScreenHeight (refer to the triggers with these names). Storyboards created in screen space are not affected by camera movement or zoom. Screen-space storyboards cannot be bound to a player.
* *stage*
This coordinate…

params.name: pos
params.description: If the storyboard is not bound, `off_x` and `off_y` specify the position at which to create the storyboard. If the storyboard is bound, `off_x` and `off_y` specify the offset from the object to which the storyboard is bound to. Has no effect in `none` space.

params.name: scale
params.description: `x_scale` and `y_scale` specify the scaling factors to apply to the storyboard in the horizontal and vertical directions. Both default to 1 (no scaling) if omitted. Has no effect in `none` space.

params.name: facing
params.description: Set facing to 1 to have the storyboard face in the same direction as the positive `off_x`, and -1 to have the storyboard face in the opposite direction. Defaults to 1. Has no effect in `none` space.

params.name: bindID
params.description: ID number of a player or helper to bind to. The position of a bound storyboard is relative to the object that it is bound to. Special values are -1 (bind to the player executing the state controller) and -2 (do not bind). Defaults to -2. The bindtime parameter is required if `bindID` is not -2. Only `stage` space storyboards can be bound.

params.name: bindtime
params.description: Specifies the number of game ticks to keep the storyboard bound. After the bindtime has expired, the storyboard will no longer be bound to the bind point, and will maintain its position. If `bind_time` is -1, then the storyboard will be bound until the storyboard is removed or another controller affects the bindtime.

sctrls.example:
type = Storyboard
trigger1 = Time = 0
path = "data/ikemen1/logo.def"
space = none

sctrls.name: SuperPause
sctrls.description: Freezes the gameplay and darkens the screen. While each player is frozen, no time passes for them. Use for a dramatic pause during the start of hyper attacks.

params.name: time
params.description: Specifies the number of ticks that the pause should last. Default is 30 ticks (half a second at default speed).

params.name: anim
params.description: Specifies the animation number (from fightfx.air) to play during the SuperPause. The default is 30, which is a charging effect. If anim is -1, no animation will be played. If you prepend `S` to *anim_no*, the animation used will be from the player's AIR file. For example, `anim = S10`.

params.name: sound
params.description: Specifies a sound to play (from common.snd) during SuperPause. The default is -1, which means no sound is played. If you prepend `S` to *snd_grp*, then the sound used will be from the player's own SND file. For example, <tt class="docutils literal">sound = S10, 0</tt>.

params.name: pos
params.description: Specifies the offset (from the player axis) at which the super anim is to be displayed. Defaults to `0, 0`.

params.name: darken
params.description: If this is 1, the screen will darken during the SuperPause. Set this to 0 to disable this effect. The default value is 1.

params.name: p2defmul
params.description: This is the amount in which to temporarily multiply the defence of any targets the player has. This is used to make chaining into supers less damaging. Setting this at 1 will make no changes to the targets' defence. 0 is a special value that will set the defence to the number set in Super.TargetDefenceMul in the [Rules] section of `mugen.cfg`. The default value is 0. Valid values are all positive numbers, including zero.

params.name: poweradd
params.description: This is the amount to add to the player's power. Defaults to 0.

params.name: unhittable
params.description: If set to 1, the player cannot be hit during the SuperPause. Set to 0 to disable this. Defaults to 1.

params.name: Brightness
params.description: Determines how much the screen should darken during the pause. Valid values are between 0 (pitch black) and 255 (no change). Defaults to 128 (same as old `darken` parameter).

sctrls.name: TagIn
sctrls.description: Makes the P1 and/or the specified partner exit `Standby` state. If no parameters are given it affects the player that called it. (Also affects helpers)

params.name: ctrl
params.description: Sets the P1 control flag.

params.name: leader
params.description: Sets the player who is considered a [team leader](triggers#new_teamleader) to the specified [playerno](triggers#new_playerno).

params.name: partnerctrl
params.description: Sets the *partner_no* control flag.

params.name: memberno
params.description: Changes the player's position in the team.

sctrls.example:
[State]
type = TagIn
trigger1 = Time = 0
leader = PlayerNo
stateno = 5600

sctrls.name: TagOut
sctrls.description:
Makes the the player and/or the specified partner enter `Standby` state. If no parameters are given it affects the player that called it. The main purpose of the `Standby` flag is to put a player away so it won't interfere in a Tag match. For that reason it carries several special properties:
* The player becomes unhittable
* The player cannot hit or push other players
* The camera will not follow the player
* `Enemy` and `P2` families of triggers will not pick up the player

params.name: self
params.description: Set to 0 to not affect P1. Defaults to 1.

params.name: partner
params.description: Specifies what teammate is afected.

params.name: stateno
params.description: The number of the state to change P1 to.

params.name: partnerstateno
params.description: The number of the state to change *partner_no* to.

params.name: memberno
params.description: Changes the player's position in the team.

sctrls.example:
[State]
type = TagOut
trigger1 = Time = 0
memberNo = 3

sctrls.name: TargetAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the player with the specified ID to the original player's target list. Do not confuse this player ID with a target ID. Target ID can be assigned with `chainID` parameter of [GetHitVarSet](sctrl#new_grthitvarset).

params.name: PlayerID
params.description: ID of player to be added.

sctrls.example: targetAdd{playerID: 60}

sctrls.name: TargetBind
sctrls.description: Binds the player's specified targets to a specified location relative to the player's axis.

params.name: time
params.description: Specifies number of ticks that this binding should be in effect. Defaults to 1.

params.name: ID
params.description: Specifies the desired target ID to bind. Only targets with this target ID will be bound. Defaults to -1 (bind all targets).

params.changeNote: This parameter now takes a third value, Specifies the offset from the player's z-axis to bind the target to.
params.name: pos
params.description: Specifies the offset from the player's axis to bind the target to. Defaults to `0, 0` if omitted.

params.name: Index
params.description: The index of the target to be affected. Defaults to -1 (all).

sctrls.name: TargetDizzyPointsAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the specified amount to all targets' dizzy points.

params.name: value
params.description: *add_amt* is added to each target's dizzy points.

params.name: ID
params.description: Specifies the desired target ID to affect. Only targets with this target ID will be affected. Defaults to -1 (affects all targets.)

sctrls.example: targetDizzyPointsAdd{value: 10; ID: -1}

sctrls.name: TargetDrop
sctrls.description: Drops all targets from the player's target list, except possibly for those having a specified target ID number. Useful for applying effects to only certain targets.

params.name: excludeID
params.description: Any targets with target ID number not equal to id_no will be dropped from the player's target list. Defaults to -1 (drop all targets).

params.name: keepone
params.description: If *keep_flag* is non-zero, then at most one target is kept on the player's target list. If there are multiple targets whose target ID number is the same as id_no, one will be picked at random and the rest will be dropped. This behavior is useful in throws, to keep from throwing multiple opponents simultaneously. If *keep_flag* is 0, then all targets with the appropriate ID number will be kept. *keep_flag* defaults to 1.

sctrls.name: TargetFacing
sctrls.description: Turns all targets to face a specified direction relative to the player.

params.name: value
params.description: If *facing_val* is positive, all targets will turn to face the same direction as the player. If *facing_val* is negative, all targets will turn to face the opposite direction as the player.

params.name: ID
params.description: Specifies the desired target ID to affect. Only targets with this target ID will be affected. Defaults to -1 (affects all targets).

params.name: Index
params.description: The index of the target to be affected. Defaults to -1 (all).

sctrls.name: TargetGuardPointsAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the specified amount to all targets' guard points.

params.name: value
params.description: *add_amt* is added to each target's guard points.

params.name: ID
params.description: Specifies the desired target ID to affect. Only targets with this target ID will be affected. Defaults to -1 (affects all targets.)

sctrls.example: targetGuardPointsAdd{value: 10; ID: -1}

sctrls.name: TargetLifeAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the specified amount to all targets' life, scaled by the targets' defense multipliers if necessary.

params.name: value
params.description: *add_amt* is added toe ach target's life.

params.name: ID
params.description: Specifies the desired target ID to affect. Only targets with this target ID will be affected. Defaults to -1 (affects all targets).

params.name: kill
params.description: If kill_flag is 0, then the addition will not take any player below 1 life point. Defaults to 1.

params.name: absolute
params.description: If *abs_flag* is 1, then *add_amt* will not be scaled (i.e. attack and defense multipliers will be ignored). Defaults to 0.

params.name: Dizzy
params.description: If set to 1, enables life to dizzy points conversion support using `Default.LifeToDizzyPointsMul` / `Super.LifeToDizzyPointsMul` const. Defaults to 1.

params.name: Index
params.description: The index of the target to be affected. Defaults to -1 (all).

sctrls.name: TargetPowerAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the specified amount to all targets' power.

params.name: value
params.description: *add_amt* is added to each target's power.

params.name: ID
params.description: Specifies the desired target ID to affect. Only targets with this target ID will be affected. Defaults to -1 (affects all targets.

params.name: Index
params.description: The index of the target to be affected. Defaults to -1 (all).

sctrls.name: TargetRedLifeAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the specified amount to all targets' red life, scaled by the targets' defense multipliers if necessary.

params.name: value
params.description: *add_amt* is added to each target's red life.

params.name: ID
params.description: Specifies the desired target ID to affect. Only targets with this target ID will be affected. Defaults to -1 (affects all targets.)

params.name: absolute
params.description: If *abs_flag* is 1, then *add_amt* will not be scaled (i.e. attack and defense multipliers will be ignored). Defaults to 0.

sctrls.example: targetRedLifeAdd{value: 10; ID: -1; absolute: 1}

sctrls.name: TargetScoreAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the specified amount of points to targets' current score counter.

params.name: value
params.description: *expr* is the the number of score points to add to the target's current score counter.

params.name: ID
params.description: Specifies the desired target ID to affect. Only targets with this target ID will be affected. Defaults to -1 (affects all targets.)

sctrls.example: targetScoreAdd{value: 100; ID: -1}

sctrls.name: TargetState
sctrls.description: Makes all targets change to the specified state number.

params.name: value
params.description: Specifies the number of the state to change the targets to.

params.name: ID
params.description: Specifies the desired target ID to affect. Only targets with this target ID will be affected. Defaults to -1 (affects all targets).

params.name: Index
params.description: The index of the target to be affected. Defaults to -1 (all).

sctrls.name: TargetVelAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the specified amounts to all targets' velocities. A positive x velocity is in the direction that the target is facing, while a positive y velocity is downward on the screen.

params.name: x
params.description: Specifies the value to add to the x-velocity of the target.

params.name: y
params.description: Specifies the value to add to the y-velocity of the target.

params.name: ID
params.description: Specifies the desired target ID to affect. Only targets with this target ID will be affected. Defaults to -1 (affects all targets).

params.name: Index
params.description: The index of the target to be affected. Defaults to -1 (all).

params.name: Z
params.description: Specifies the value to add to the target's z-velocity.

sctrls.example:
; Applies constant gravity to all targets  
type = TargetVelAdd  
trigger1 = 1  
y = 0.45

sctrls.name: TargetVelSet

params.name: x

params.name: y
params.description: Specifies the value to set the y-velocity of the target to.

params.name: ID
params.description: Specifies the desired target ID to affect. Only targets with this target ID will be affected. Defaults to -1 (affects all targets).

params.name: Index

sctrls.name: Text
sctrls.description: Text controller is used for displaying text on screen.

params.name: removetime
params.description: The text will be removed after having been displayed for *rem_time* number of game ticks. Defaults to 1.

params.name: layerno
params.description: Sets the layer to which the text will be drawn on. 0 is in front of the background, but behind the players. 1 is in front of the players, but behind the foreground. 2 is in front of the foreground. Defaults to 1.

params.name: localcoord
params.description: Sets custom localcoord. If omitted, lifebar font defaults to the lifebar localcoord, character font and debug font defaults to the screen localcoord.

params.name: text
params.description: Text to be rendered. Defaults to "%v" (rendering first *params* argument of any type). *format_string* must be encased in double-quotes. It is a *printf* format string. You can use \t to generate a tab character (tab width is equivalent to 4 characters) and \n to break lines. To display the value of an arithmetic expression, you can put a %d (for ints) or a %f (for floats) in the format string, then specify the expression in the params list. To display a % character, you must put %% in the format string. Accepted format specifiers: %v (any type), %d, %i, %f, %F, %e, %E, %g, or %G. Syntax such as %0.2f is also supported.

params.name: params
params.description: Unlimited amount of numeric arguments can be specified in the format string. These should be listed under the params item, in order. The type of each parameter must match its format specifier.

params.name: font
params.description: *font_no* specifies the number of the font to use for text rendering. The 'F' prefix is optional: if included, then the text is rendred using lifebar (fight.def) fonts. Otherwise font [declared](https://github.com/ikemen-engine/Ikemen-GO/wiki/Character-features#def_files_font) in character's DEF file is used. If specified font doesn't exist than the debug font is used. Defaults to debug font.

params.name: bank
params.description: Color bank of the font to use. Refer to the font for what color banks it has. Defaults to 0.

params.name: align
params.description: *alignment* is a number representing the text alignment. 1 is left, 0 means center, and -1 is for right-alignment. Defaults to 1.

params.name: angle
params.description: Specify the rotation, rotation point is based on the text's alignment. Defaults to 0.

params.name: pos
params.description: Specify the offset at which to create the text. Defaults to 0,0.

params.name: scale
params.description: Specify the scaling factors to apply to the text in the horizontal and vertical directions. Defaults to 1,1.

params.name: color
params.description: Color adjustment values for the font. Defaults to 256,256,256,256 (no color adjustment).

params.name: id
params.description: Specifies an ID number for this text. Used to identify particular text in numText trigger and removeText sctrl.

params.name: textspacing
params.description: Specifies extra spacing between letters (*x_spacing*) and extra spacing between lines when `\n` is used to break lines (*y_spacing*). These values are added on top of the font’s DEF Spacing values.

params.name: textdelay
params.description: Adjusts the text typing time, the longer the time the longer the delay between each letter typed.

params.name: velocity
params.description: Applies speed to text on the defined axis.

params.name: accel
params.description: Applies acceleration to text on the defined axis.

params.name: friction
params.description: Applies friction to text on the defined axis (Friction value example: 0.95).

params.name: xshear
params.description: Specifies the amount of horizontal shearing to apply to the text. Defaults to 0.

params.name: maxdist
params.description:
Specifies the maximum velocity beyond which additional velocity will no longer be applied. Defaults to 0 (unlimited).

**palfx.key** The text sctrl can accept all the same key values from [PalFX state controller](http://www.elecbyte.com/mugendocs/sctrls.html#palfx)

params.name: hidewithbars
params.description: Enabling this parameter hides the text automatically when the fight screen is hidden.

sctrls.name: Trans
sctrls.description: Overrides the player's animation transparency parameters for current game tick. Useful for special effects.
changeNotes: Ikemen GO has some expanded transparency options. Note: Applies to all `trans` definitions (e.g. explods, backgrounds, etc).

params.name: trans
params.description:
*trans_type* must be one of the following:

- default: does nothing
- none: disables transparency
- add: draws with additive transparency (`alpha` defaults to `256,256`)
- addalpha: deprecated in 1.1; draws with additive transparency (`alpha` defaults to `256,0`)
- add1: deprecated in 1.1; draws with additive transparency (`alpha` defaults to `256,128`)
- sub: draws with full subtractive transparency (`alpha` is fixed at `256,256`)

params.name: alpha
params.description: These are the source and destination alpha values for the add trans types. Valid values are from 0 (low) to 256 (high). If omitted, default depends on *trans_type*.

params.name: Sub
params.description: The `sub` transparency now also supports alpha values.

params.name: SubAdd
params.description: The `subadd` transparency mode was added. It draws the sprite in grayscale subtractive transparency, then draws it again in full color additive transparency. The result is a transparent effect that looks more solid and is easier to see against bright backgrounds. The `alpha` source parameter controls the intensity of the additive layer, while destination controls the subtractive layer. Native implementation of a classic Mugen trick.

sctrls.example:
; Fades the character in, over 256 ticks.  
type = Trans  
trigger1 = time < 256  
trans = add  
alpha = time, 256-time

sctrls.name: TransformClsn
sctrls.description: Changes the geometry or certain properties of the player's collision boxes.

params.name: group
params.description: The type of collision box to transform. Valid values: `All`, `None`, `Clsn1`, `Clsn2`, `Size` and `Dummy`. Using `None` removes all active modifiers. Defaults to `None`.

params.name: index
params.description: Determines the index of the collision box to transform. Use `-1` for all of them.

params.name: scale
params.description: Scale multiplier to be applid to the boxes.

params.name: angle
params.description: Changes the angle of the boxes. In degrees.

params.name: pivot
params.description: Determines the angle's rotation center.

sctrls.name: TransformSprite
sctrls.description: Apply certain deformations to the char's sprite.

params.name: window
params.description: The window parameter forms a rectangle (similar to clsn) relative to the char, outside of which pixels will not be drawn.

params.name: xshear
params.description: Specifies the amount of horizontal shearing to apply to the char. Defaults to 0.

params.name: projection
params.description:
Valid values:
- `orthographic` (default)
- `perspective` (distortion relative to the center of the screen)
- `perspective2` (distortion relative to the sprite)

Affects how the char sprite is drawn when `xangle` or `yangle` is not zero.

params.name: focallength
params.description: Focal Length of the projection. Does nothing when projection is not perspective or perspective2.

sctrls.name: Turn
sctrls.description: Instantly turns the player to face the opposite direction. Does not play a turning animation.

sctrls.name: VarAdd
sctrls.description: Adds to one of the player's working variables. Either a float variable or an int variable can be added to by this controller.

params.name: v
params.description: *var_no* specifies the number of the variable to affect. It must evaluate to an integer between 0 and 59.

params.name: value
params.description:
*int_expr* specifies the value to add to the int variable indexed by *var_no*.

*float_expr* is the value to add to the float variable indexed by *var_no*.

params.name: fv
params.description: *var_no* specifies the number of the variable to affect. It must evaluate to an integer between 0 and 39.

sctrls.name: VarRandom
sctrls.description: Sets the specified int variable to a random value. Float variables cannot be set by this controller.

params.name: v
params.description: *var_no* is the index of the int variable to affect. It must evaluate to an integer between 0 and 59.

params.name: range
params.description: *least_val* and *greatest_val* specify the least and greatest values which can be assigned by this controller, respectively. The value assigned to the variable will be a randomly chosen integer from this range. *range* defaults to `0, 1000`. If only one argument is specified, that is considered to specify the range 0,(argument).

sctrls.example:
;Assign a random number between 0 and 500 to var(5).  
type = VarRandom  
v = 5  
range = 500

sctrls.name: VarRangeSet
sctrls.description: Sets a contiguous range of the player's working variables to the same value. Either float variables or int variables can be set by this controller, but not both at the same time.

params.name: value
params.description: *int_expr* is evaluated once to give the value that is assigned to all int variables in the range.

params.name: fvalue
params.description: *float_expr* is evaluated once to give the value that is assigned to all float variables in the range.

params.name: first
params.description: Specifies the lower end of the range of variables to set. Defaults to 0 (first variable).

params.name: last
params.description: Specifies the higher end of the range of variables to set. Defaults to 59 for int variables, or 39 for float variables (this is the last available variable in both cases).

sctrls.name: VarSet
sctrls.description: Sets one of the player's working variables. Either a float variable or an int variable can be set by this controller, but not both at the same time.

params.name: v
params.description: *var_no* specifies the number of the variable to affect. It must evaluate to an integer between 0 and 59.

params.name: value
params.description:
*int_expr* specifies the value to assign to the int variable indexed by *var_no*.

*float_expr* is the value to assign to the float variable indexed by *var_no*.

params.name: fv
params.description: *var_no* specifies the number of the variable to affect. It must evaluate to an integer between 0 and 39.

sctrls.name: VelAdd
sctrls.description: Adds the specified amounts to the player's velocity. A positive x velocity is in the direction that the player is facing, while a positive y velocity is downward on the screen.

params.name: x
params.description: Specifies the value to add to the player's x-velocity.

params.name: y
params.description: Specifies the value to add to the player's y-velocity.

sctrls.example:
; Applies constant gravity to the player  
trigger1 = 1  
type = VelAdd  
y = 0.45

sctrls.name: VelMul
sctrls.description: Multiplies the player's velocity by the specified amounts. A positive x velocity is in the direction that the player is facing, while a positive y velocity is downward on the screen.

params.name: x
params.description: Specifies the value to multiply the player's x-velocity with.

params.name: y
params.description: Specifies the value to multiply the player's y-velocity with.

sctrls.example:
; Applies constant friction to the player  
trigger1 = 1  
type = VelMul  
x = 0.8

sctrls.name: VelSet
sctrls.description: Sets the player's velocity to the specified values. A positive x velocity is in the direction that the player is facing, while a positive y velocity is downward on the screen.

params.name: x
params.description: Specifies the value to assign to the player's x-velocity.

params.name: y
params.description: Specifies the value to assign to the player's y-velocity.

sctrls.name: VictoryQuote
sctrls.description: Selects a victory quote from the player to display in the next victory screen.

params.name: value
params.description: Specifies the index of the quote to use.  Valid index values are from 0 to 99. If *quote_index* evaluates to an invalid index, a random quote will be selected. Defaults to -1.

sctrls.name: Width
sctrls.description: Temporarily changes the size of the player's width bar for 1 tick. Useful for controlling the `pushing` behavior when the player makes contact with another or with the sides of the screen.

params.name: edge
params.description: Sets the player's edge width in front and behind. Edge width determines how close the player can get to the edge of the screen. These parameters default to `0, 0` if omitted.

params.name: player
params.description: Sets the player width in front and behind. Player width determines how close the player can get to other players. These parameters default to `0, 0` if omitted.

params.name: value
params.description: This is a shorthand syntax for setting both edge width and player width simultaneously. This may only be used if the edge and player parameters are not specified.

sctrls.name: Zoom
changeNotes: Zoom was a beta feature in Mugen 1.1. It is a fully functional state controller in Ikemen GO.

params.name: CameraBound
params.description: If set to 1, the zoom position is restricted to the current camera position. Defaults to 1.

params.name: EndLag
params.description: Like the `lag` parameter, but it applies after the Zoom effect ends.

params.name: Lag
params.description: Controls the smoothing effect for camera position and scale transitions during zoom, with smaller values leading to quicker adjustments and larger values causing more gradual changes. Valid values are between 0 and 1, where 0 snaps the camera instantly and 1 delays the zoom effect indefinitely. Defaults to 0.

params.name: Pos
params.description: The position on screen to bind the zoom, relative to the center of the screen. A value of Pos X, Pos Y will zoom in on P1.

params.name: Scale
params.description: The camera zoom factor as a float. Values greater than 1 zoom in, while values between 0 and 1 zoom out. For example, a value of 2 doubles the size of the sprites.

params.name: StageBound
params.description: If set to 1, the zoom position is restricted to the stage boundaries. Defaults to 1.

params.name: Time
params.description: Countdown timer that controls how long zoom effects are applied, decreasing by 1 every frame. Once it reaches 0, the zoom stops, and the camera resets to its default behavior without any smoothing or zoom effects. Defaults to 1.
